# Fuaran.Core — decisions (newest first)

Each entry is a `## <date> — D<n>: <title>` heading with a status line under it, which says how
far the ruling stands:

- **`Live`** — it stands as written, including any amendment its own body records.
- **`Amended-by D<n>`** — a later entry changes part of it; read the two together.
- **`Superseded-by D<n>`** — a later entry replaces it whole.
- **`Moved-to-compute`** — it governs code that
  [`fuaran-core-compute`](https://github.com/Fuaran-Core/fuaran-core-compute) produces since `0.33.0`
  (D66, D71); the record stays here as written.
- **`Never-minted`** — no decision carries the number.

Clauses combine with `; ` (`Moved-to-compute; Amended-by D21`), and text after ` — ` is a note. Entries
sit newest first by date, so the ordinals within one day are not always in order; the index below is
in ordinal order. It is generated from the headings and their status lines, and `DecisionsTests` holds
it equal to them. [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) says how an entry is added.

## 2026-10-21 — D204: the graph questions are asked once, in `Fuaran.Core.Relation` — a relation prepared once over any comparable node, its answers functions of the edge set, and `Propagation` byte-identical over it; the model is scheduled, not declined

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 552. A new package, `Fuaran.Core.Relation`, FSharp.Core-only and Fable-clean; `Fuaran.Core.Propagation` gains a project reference and loses its private Tarjan and frontier closure, every public name and every answer unchanged. Additive: it rides the `0.40.0` draft slot (docs/releases/0.40.0.md), which is untagged (`v0.39.0` is the last tag) and pinned by no public-path consumer. Hand-numbered: the take reserved no number for this phase, so this is the record's newest plus one at the time of writing.**

*The premise, checked.* Four implementations of one question lived across this repository and three downstream consumers: this repository's `Propagation` (a private iterative Tarjan, Phase 298, over `Map<string, Set<string>>`), a downstream program-tier library's `Relation` (generic over `'N : comparison`, over `Map<'N, 'N list>`, with a law set against brute-force references), a downstream tooling library's `cyclesAmong` / `survivorsAmong` (a recursive Tarjan over string-keyed list maps, plus calls into the program tier's `Relation`), and a downstream code generator's cycle grouping (Tarjan over `System.Type` keyed by REFERENCE identity, for contiguous recursive groups). Each was read for the surface it needs, and the API below is sized to those four and to nothing guessed:

| Caller | Input shape | Asks for |
|---|---|---|
| `Propagation` (here) | `Map<string, Set<string>>`, dangling reads filtered first | the sort (`Order` + `Cycles`, each cycle's members in the walker's pop order), the cycle through an id, the inverse as a map, the closure over the inverse (dirty) and over the relation (needed) |
| the program tier's `Relation` | `Map<'N, 'N list>` | `components` (members ascending), `cycles`, `cyclesAmong`, `reachable`, `terminals` |
| the tooling library | `Map<string, string list>` | `cyclesAmong`; `survivorsAmong` = `terminals` returning a first-reached LIST, an unknown id ending at itself |
| the code generator | edges between `System.Type`, reference identity | the components and whether each is a cycle, in finish order |

*Decided: generic over `'N : comparison`, with no string-keyed convenience layer.* `Propagation` keys ids by their `IdWitness` string form to stay generic over an `'Id` without `comparison` — but at the relation the ids ARE strings, and `string` is comparable, so the string caller needs nothing the generic one does not give. The other three callers are comparable too (strings, or an index the generator already assigns each type: a caller keyed by reference identity numbers its nodes and runs the package over `int`). The comparison is what the package USES — it sorts the dense form and finds a node by binary search — so nothing is hashed: no `Dictionary`, no `HashIdentity.Structural`, nothing whose Fable semantics would have to be argued. That is the Fable-clean posture bought by construction rather than by a check.

*Decided: a relation is PREPARED once (`Relation<'N>`, by `ofMap`), and every question reads the prepared form.* Each question is then `O(N + E)`; the one `O((N + E) log N)` — building the sorted node array and binary-searching each successor — is paid at `ofMap`, once. A caller that asks several questions of one relation (`Propagation.plan`, a tooling index that asks for cycles and survivors of one graph) prepares once. `ofMap` takes `Map<'N, 'S>` for any `'S :> seq<'N>`, so the set-valued and the list-valued callers above both pass what they hold; the keys and every successor are the nodes, a repeated successor is one edge, and the input's order never reaches an answer.

*Decided: the members of a component come out in the pass's POP ORDER, not sorted.* This is the choice the byte-identity requirement forces, and it is the better contract regardless. `Propagation`'s `Cycles` have always listed each group in Tarjan's stack order (its `TopoResult` doc says so), every consumer's golden and every law vector carries that order, and the pass is deterministic over ascending nodes with ascending successors, so pop order is a function of the edge set exactly as a sorted list is. It carries more: for a simple cycle the members reversed are the cycle's PATH, each consecutive pair an edge — what a rejection envelope enumerates (GP5) — where sorting destroys the path. The program tier's `Relation`, which documents members ascending, sorts each list in its forward (a `List.sort` per component) when its successor phase re-points it here; that is the one visible difference between the two surfaces, and it is theirs to keep or drop on their untagged draft.

*Decided: `inverse`, not `dependents`.* The package is domain-neutral; "dependents" is `Propagation`'s reading of the inverse over a "depends on" relation, and `Propagation.dependents` keeps that name over `Relation.inverse |> Relation.toMap`, filtered to the ids something reads (its `Plan` field has always said an id nothing reads has no key). `reachable` over the inverse is the dirty set; `reachable` over the relation is the needed set; the frontier closure `Propagation` kept for both is deleted, since the same traversal answers both.

*Decided: `terminals` answers a SET, and an unknown node ends at itself.* The program tier's contract, kept: the tooling library's `survivorsAmong` answers a first-reached list, and the order of that list is an accident of its recursion that nothing downstream should read; its adoption phase takes the set.

*Decided: `work` is internal, granted to the test project.* The pass's counted work — nodes finished plus edges examined — is the evidence the linearity law reads (`work = N + E` on every drawn relation) and nothing a consumer needs; it joins the grants the friend-grant paragraph of STABILITY.md counts. The cost claim is stated honestly, as the program tier's D47 stated it: the PASS is linear; preparing the form is `O((N + E) log N)`, which is what a canonical answer over a comparable node costs.

*Decided: `Propagation` delegates and is held byte-identical by a differential, not by inspection.* `Propagation.sort` removes dangling reads first (they were never nodes: an edge to an id the map does not hold is a validator defect, not a cycle) and prepares the rest, so the relation's nodes are exactly the map's keys, visited ascending with ascending reads — the walk the Phase-298 walker always made. `RelationTests` keeps that walker whole, with the old `sort`, `dependents` and `closureOver`, as the reference, and holds `Propagation.sort` (`Order`, `Cycles` and each cycle's member order), `dependents`, `dirtyFromChangedIds` and `neededFor` equal to it on four hundred seeded maps with dangling reads and self-reads. Every existing `Propagation` test passes unchanged, the `validTopo` certificate holds on every map, and `proofs/Propagation.fst` still takes `sort` as a parameter — fuaran-core#553 is where the SCC specification itself is proved, after which `Propagation.fst` stops parameterising it and this package's `model-scheduled` entry in `proofs/coverage-exclusions.json` is deleted. Until then its eleven operations are `measured-elsewhere` with `RelationTests` as the stand-in.

*The law set is the program tier's, ported.* Every cycle is found (each edge whose target reaches its source has both ends in `cyclesAmong`); a node is on a cycle exactly when it reaches itself; two nodes share a component exactly when each reaches the other and the components partition the nodes; cycles are the non-trivial components in the components' order; reordering and repeating successor lists moves no answer; components come dependencies-first; `reachable`, `inverse`, `sort` and `terminals` equal their definitions; the counted work is exactly `N + E`. Regressions: the dense diamond (200 layers, 4 wide, `4^200` paths) in linear work with and without its back edge, and a chain and a ring of 200,000 nodes answered without exhausting the stack (the recursive form `Propagation` replaced in Phase 298 died near 3,500 deep in Debug and 13,700 in Release). **Go-red, recorded:** dropping the on-stack low-link update in the pass (`low[v] <- min low[v] order[w]` for a successor on the stack — the line that makes a back edge a cycle) turned eleven of the twenty tests red, "every cycle is found" and the Phase-298 differential among them, and the restored line turned all twenty green; a first attempt at the perturbation that missed its line left all twenty green, which is why the probe was re-run until the diff showed the edit.

*A premise of the phase was false, and is recorded rather than built against.* The phase named `tests/fable-smoke/` as a directory to create and extend. It left this repository at Phase 217 (D55): the Fable compiler belongs to the consumer that owns a Fable toolchain, the smoke is that consumer's `tests/core-fable/`, and `FableSmokeCompletenessTests` holds that no script here invokes `dotnet fable`. Re-creating the directory would reverse a recorded decision and redden the gate. The claim is made the way this repository makes it: the package ships the `fable/` source distribution (the `Directory.Build.props` default the completeness test holds), and the worker compiled the package and the delegating `Propagation` under Fable 5 from a scratch project outside the tree, which is reported in the phase's outcome, not committed. **The smoke line this change needs in the receiving gate**, per STABILITY.md "The portability set": a `PackageReference` to `Fuaran.Core.Relation` in that consumer's `CoreFable.fsproj` and `Directory.Packages.props`, and in its `Program.fs` one touch of `Relation.ofMap |> Relation.sort`, `Relation.cyclesAmong`, `Relation.reachable`, `Relation.inverse` and `Relation.terminals` beside the existing `Propagation` block. That consumer's cut-time run checks membership against the candidate's packages, so the line lands before `0.40.0` is tagged.

*The adoption plan, by caller.* (1) The program tier's `Relation` becomes a forward to this package — `ofMap` over its list-valued map, a `List.sort` per component to keep its ascending-members contract or a documented switch to pop order — before its draft is tagged; it already pins `Fuaran.Core.*`. (2) The tooling library's `cyclesAmong` becomes `Relation.ofMap >> Relation.cyclesAmong` and `survivorsAmong` becomes `Relation.terminals` with the set read where the list was; its verb host's three calls into the program tier's `Relation` move here, which keeps that library program-free. (3) The code generator numbers its planned types by position (it already holds that index) and runs `Relation.components` over `int`, reading `isCycle` as "more than one member or a self-edge" exactly as it does today; that generator's repository conforms to and consumes this one's public packages, never the reverse. Each is its own phase on its own side; none is in this one.

## 2026-10-21 — D203: the oracle's differential is one harness — a declared tally, one seeded loop, a render pair per answer DU and the go-red arm — and a go-red is proven by the harness losing

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 535. Tests only; rides the `0.40.0` draft (docs/releases/0.40.0.md, Internal). No package or wire surface moves.**

*Decided: one harness.* `Differential<'P,'M>` (the render pair) and `Tally` live in `tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/ProofOracle.Bridges.fs`; the per-file tally records, empty values and hand loops are gone.

*Decided: the tally is declared.* An undeclared counter, set or finding class fails the test, because a misspelt counter reading zero would let an equality between two of them hold vacuously.

*Decided: the loop is generic over the generator state* rather than fixing `ConfRng`, so every pool kept its seed and draw order and every count its value.

*Decided: an in-pass go-red instrument.* A go-red instrument run in the agreement's own pass records under its own class (`Tally.goRed`), read by the go-red arm and not by the agreement arm.

*Decided: the converters stay per model.* The to/of-model converters are the bridge, the chain's third link, not copies of the loop; only duplicates were removed.

*Decided: a verdict DU compared as a class* (Phase 147) is compared by value through `Differential.check`, never through a render.

*The evidence.* A harness planted to drop every finding turns every model's go-red red and no agreement case.

## 2026-10-21 — D202: a record whose only content is "nothing" is deleted, not kept — the doc-comment ratchet at zero becomes the invariant, the inert open-phase list and the scheduled half of coverage clause 2 go until a writer exists, and the release sequence is the contract, not the procedure

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 537. Test projects and records only; rides the `0.40.0` draft (docs/releases/0.40.0.md, Internal). No package surface, wire byte or conformance file moves.**

*Decided: the doc-comment ratchet (Phase 339).* `docs/doc-coverage.json` held, per package, the public members allowed to be undocumented. Every one of its twenty lists was empty, so the file stated one invariant as twenty rows of data, with an approval stem, a reader, a writer and a contributor-table row of its own. It is deleted with all four, and `PackageDocsTests` asserts the invariant directly: no public member of a packable package without a doc comment, each finding naming the package and the member's documentation id. A member that genuinely cannot carry a comment is a compiler-written token class, skipped by `docId` and listed with its reason in that file's header. `CORE_APPROVE_DOCS` stays: it governs `DECISIONS`, `ledger-index`, `fantomasignore`, `version-derives`, `copies`, `CONTRIBUTING` and `idl-schema`. Revisit when a package must ship an undocumented member: that is the moment for an allowance, held by name, not before.

*Decided: the open-phase list (Phase 294, D75; Phase 400).* `tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/open-phases.json` was declared inert from the day it was written, and no row ever made the scheduling claim it existed to check. It is deleted with its reader, the scheduled arm of coverage clause 2, the `scheduled` bucket of the predicate line and the test that read `FUARAN_CORE_ROADMAP` to prove it unread. A `model-bridge`'s `closes` is drawn from `permanent` and `unscheduled`, in the ladder (`bridge-closes`) and in clause 2 alike; a phase is refused as a value no check in this repository can evaluate. Revisit when something outside this repository writes a list of this side's open phases: the scheduled half returns with that writer, holding the list it writes.

*Decided: the release wording.* `RELEASING.md` says the sequence in `STABILITY.md` "Versioning policy" is the CONTRACT a release honours, and that the release act is performed by tooling outside this repository whose preflight re-reads the packed public surfaces. It names no tool. Its own restated summary of the sequence and `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s partial packing procedure are removed, so the sequence is written once. `docs/conformance-corpus.md`'s "Moving `<Version>`" sequence stays: it is the detail of the contract's step 1, which cites it, and governs every `<Version>` move, not only a release.

*Also.* `ComputeBoundaryTests`' hand list of the spine is read from `Roster.derive`, and its tree test holds that every project under `src/` ships. `KitRoster` carries one roster rather than a one-element list; a composition of rosters returns with a second share.

*Rejected.* Keeping the ratchet file as data in case coverage regresses by package (a regression is red by name either way, and an empty allowance list cannot record anything a test does not already hold); keeping the open-phase list inert (a clause that cannot fire until a writer exists is a promise in the tree, and the README already says no schedule is kept); naming the release tool in `RELEASING.md` (the publication boundary forbids it, and the contract is what a reader of this repository can check).

*Amends D75.* Its "the scheduling clause reads data, not an environment variable" paragraph is superseded: neither the data file nor the clause half remains.

**Recorded by Phase 532. `tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests.Fixtures` and `tools/Fuaran.Core.Tools` (new; neither is packed), the test project, `proofs/check.ps1`, `proofs/oracle/Fuaran.Core.Proofs.Oracle.fsproj`, the projection registry and the records it renders, and one `InternalsVisibleTo` grant in `Fuaran.Core.Conformance`; rides the `0.40.0` draft (Internal: no package surface moves). Amends D74.**

*Decided: the test runner has no verb.* `tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/Program.fs` carried a dozen flags, and
six of the eight exporters behind them were sub-modules of test files, so running the suite and writing
the corpus were one assembly's two jobs. Now there are three projects. The fixtures library
(`tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests.Fixtures`) holds what both readers need. That is the reference domains and the
certification vocabularies (`MiniIdl`, `ReferenceIdl`, `SecondDomainIdl`, `ScoreDomainIdl` and the
decode, refusal-corner, derivation and spec-decoder ones), the exporter table and its eight exporters, the
generators of every committed module, `ChildProcess` and `Repo`, `Approval`, `KitRoster`, `Roster` (what
ships) and the proof leg's ladder check, coverage predicate and cone selector. The test project references
it and holds what is generated. The tool references it and writes. It holds no test: the runner discovers
only its own assembly, and the `Fixtures` family holds that.

*Decided: one verb renders, over one table.* `render <family> [<dir>]`: `laws`, `apply`, `refusals`,
`decode`, `escape`, `encoding`, `families`, `generated` (the nine committed F# modules and the spike
snapshot), `idl-classify-fixtures`, `fstar` (the six models and the vectors module) and `oracle-project`.
`Renders.names` is the table. A projection-registry row's `render` names a family. The `Projections`
family holds the two to each other in both directions, by reference rather than by reading `Program.fs`
as text. The command is spelt once, in `Tool.fs`. Every remedy a drift guard prints, and every record the
registry renders (`copies.json`'s `regen`, `version-derives.json`'s `emit`), is built from that one
spelling. The eight hand copies of the old invocation became that one. `proof-cone` takes the arguments
`--proof-cone` took. `proofs/check.ps1` builds the tool and names the verb, so a repository that adopted
the kit is untouched: the caller, not the kit, names it. The bytes of every artefact are unchanged: each
was pinned before the move and compared after it, emitted through the tool, and a planted change to an
exporter moved its pin.

*Decided: `--idl-diff` is retired.* `fuaran-core-idl classify` (`Fuaran.Core.Idl.Cli`) is the one
command that classifies two `idl.json` revisions. The runner's copy printed `Diff.run`'s text with exit
0/1 beside it.

*Decided: the oracle project's `Compile` list is generated.* `render oracle-project` writes it from
`proofs/modules.json`, every extracted and shared module in check order, between two markers below the
hand-written runtime floor. `Proofs.Ladder` holds the committed file to that render, and still holds each
module after every module it opens. The per-model comments the list carried restated `modules.json`'s
notes and are gone.

*Amended: D74, placement only.* "The cone is computed in the test project beside `parseModules`" no
longer holds. The ladder check (`ProofLadder`), the cone selector (`ProofCone`) and the oracle project's
render read the roster through ONE function, `ProofLadder.parseRoster`, in the fixtures library. That is
the property D74 protected, kept. The cone is still recomputed from the tree every time, and nothing about
the cache D74 declined changes. `check.ps1` asks the tool instead of the test project.

*Decided, and kept as a dependency: the reference run measures the families export.* The `families`
row's `cases` column is the conformance reference run (`ConformanceVacuityTests.cases`, Phase 196). Its
witnesses and generators are the suite's own, defined across about twenty test files. So the exporter
table takes that one measurement as an argument (`Exporters.tableWith`), and the tool references the test
project to pass it. Moving the witnesses would be a second move of a size this one does not take; it is
not a placement of the tool. *Revisit when* the reference run's witnesses join the fixtures library. The
reference then drops, and nothing else changes.

*Decided: an approval switch stays in the suite.* `CORE_APPROVE_*` and `FUARAN_REGEN` rewrite a
projection from inside the test that renders and compares it (Phase 396's one reading). The renderers
behind them (the reflected API and wire surfaces, the README regions, the decision and ledger indexes)
live with the families that hold them. A switch is the operator admitting a change the family just
measured. It is not a generator the gate could run, so a switch remains a deliberate act. The registry
still names each one, and a row with a switch and no `render` is regenerated by its family.

*Declined: the release ledger and the decisions parser in the fixtures library.* The plan for this move listed
`Ledger` among the fixtures because a tool was to render the ledger index. That index is approval-written
(above), so nothing the tool does reads the ledger, and `Ledger.fs` stays with its family. It would carry
the decisions parser with it.

*What the gate does is unchanged.* `verify.ps1` builds the solution, which now includes both projects. It
runs the suite and never the tool. Its format check names `src tests samples`, so the tool's single source
file is formatted with the rest but not yet checked by the gate. The one-word widening is an operator
edit, because the gate script is not a worker's to change.

## 2026-10-20 — D200: the seams' refusal and declaration codecs are derived from their IDL declaration; the hand codecs and strict rosters go, a decode refusal reads itself back in `Wire`, and a strict reader of an undeclared tag answers `UnknownTag`

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 551. `Fuaran.Core.Function`, `Fuaran.Core.Query`, `Fuaran.Core.Column`, `Fuaran.Core.AiSurface`, `Fuaran.Core.Wire`, `Fuaran.Core.Conformance`; rides the `0.40.0` draft (STABILITY.md, "The generated layer is printed from ONE resolution"). Applies D195 and D198, and amends D195.**

*Decided: the nine unions are declared in the IDL, and their codecs are generated.* `InvokeError` with
`DeclarationFault`, `Placement` with `IslandKind`, `Deferred<'T>`, `ArgSource` / `PipelineNode` with the
pipeline record, `QueryError` with `ColumnPredicate`, `SortKey` with `SortDirection`, `FieldChange` (whose
discriminator is `member`) and `Rejection<'Id>` with `NestRelation` are declared once, under `LowerFirst`, in
`tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/SeamIdl.fs`. The types stay hand-declared (D195). Five codec-only modules are
committed beside the types they serve (`CapabilitySeamCodec` and `PipelineSeamCodec` in `Function`,
`QuerySeamCodec` in `Query`, `FieldChangeSeamCodec` in `Column`, `RejectionSeamCodec` in `AiSurface`). Each
carries a `projections.json` row, a stamp and a `.fantomasignore` line, and is held by a drift guard. Its
`encode<Name>` / `decode<Name>` / `decode<Name>Strict` are public, and they are the JVal-level entries that
replace the removed `invokeErrorJson` / `invokeErrorOf`, `deferredJson` / `deferredOf` / `deferredOfWith`,
`queryErrorJson` / `queryErrorOf` and `RejectionCodec.encode`. The seams' text forms (`encodeInvokeError`,
`decodeDeferred`, `decodeDeferredWith`, `encodeQueryError`, `RejectionCodec.render` and the rest) keep their
names and their bytes. Each union's cases are declared in the order its reader always named them, so an
unknown tag's sentence lists the tags as before. A codec-only module is placed between its types and its
callers, which split three files: `CapabilityCodec.fs` from `Capability.fs`, `CapabilityPipelineTypes.fs`
from `CapabilityPipeline.fs`, and `QueryTypes.fs` from `Query.fs`. A module and a type that share a name
across files carry `ModuleSuffix` explicitly, so their compiled names do not move.

*Decided: what the IDL does not model is a typed hosted slot.* A value space is `SpaceCodec`'s (a pipeline
node's output space through `PipelineWire.outputSpace`, which keeps Phase 307's admission check). A column
type, a predicate kind and a comparison's literal are `QueryWire`'s; the literal is a case-level host codec
over `ColumnCodec.readCell` / `writeCell` (D198). A unit is `Unit.render` / `Unit.parse`. A decode refusal is
`DecodeError.toJson` and the new `DecodeError.decoder`, which moves the query seam's private reader into
`Wire` and reads a stored `message` back verbatim, so a journalled refusal replays as written (D188).
An invocation argument's `(addr, source)` pair is a hosted slot over the generated `ArgSource` codec, and
the strict reading leaves it to its reader, as it leaves every hosted slot (D198).

*Decided (driver ruling 2026-10-20): a strict reader of a tag its union does not declare answers
`UnknownTag` at the discriminator.* The hand roster `QueryShape.predicateMembers` gave an unknown predicate
tag the comparison roster, so a strict read of `{"$type":"like","text":…}` was refused `UndeclaredMember` at
`text`. A derived roster exists only for a declared case, so the strict read answers what the lenient read
answers. The same holds for an unknown `Placement` tag carrying a member. A seam's strict reading is now the
derived reader's, applied where the value is read: the declaration's own members are checked first, then
its placement, predicates and sort keys are read strictly in decode order. So a document carrying both an
undeclared member there and a fault read earlier is refused at the earlier fault. Both moves are pinned
(`FunctionTests` / `QueryTests`, the Phase 551 rows). Every other pinned code and path, every document byte
and both capture journals are unchanged. Three rows move their SENTENCE alone, and are re-pinned under D188:
an unknown enum value reads `unknown case '<v>' of enum '<E>'`, and the schema delta's `amended.member` and
`amended.to` refusals carry the derived decoder's sentences.

*Decided: the seam-refusal family.* `Conformance.seamRefusalLaws` holds every generated entry to authored
vectors: each document read back to its own bytes, or refused with its code at its path. It covers every
case of every union and each strict reader's undeclared member. `conformance/refusals/seam-refusals.json`
exports the vectors with the refusals manifest's `seamRefusals` row. Core-internal: no corpus copy carries
it (D163 placed the family with this derivation).

*Decided: a codec-only module documents itself.* The generator prints a `///` line before `module`, naming
the roots its request covers, so the module type is documented like every public member.

AMENDS D195: its "hand codecs deleted, strict rosters derived" is done, and its strict readers answer with
the precedence above.

## 2026-10-20 — D198: the IDL states what a derived seam codec needs. A union declares its tag-naming rule; a hosted codec declares whether its refusal is typed; a union case may declare a case-level host codec; a codec-only module derives codecs over host-declared types; and a strict-members reading refuses an undeclared member at it

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 550. `Fuaran.Core.Idl`, `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen`; rides the `0.40.0` draft (STABILITY.md, "The generated layer is printed from ONE resolution"). Amends D163 and D195.**

*Decided: the tag-naming rule is a field of the union declaration.* `IdlUnion.TagRule` is a closed
`UnionTagRule`: `CaseName` (the wire tag is the case name, every union declared before) or `LowerFirst`
(D163's seam rule: `NoSuchCapability` is written `noSuchCapability`). `IdlUnionCase.Tag` is the case NAME,
and the wire carries `IdlUnion.WireTagOf` of it. Every reader takes the tag from that one member: the
interpreter (`Encode`, `Decode`, `Sample`), the F#, TypeScript and F* emitters, the JSON schema and the
TypeScript declarations. An `IdlValue.VUnion` carries the WIRE tag, as `VEnum` carries the wire string, and
only the F# emitter maps it back to the case. `idl.json` writes `tagRule` only away from `caseName`, so every
existing artifact is byte-identical. `Declare.errors` refuses two cases of one union that derive one wire tag
(`Abc` and `abc` under `lowerFirst`). The stability classifier classes a rule change `breaking-wire`
(`UnionTagRuleChanged`). The rule was placed on the declaration, not keyed by name on a vocabulary-level
record as `TransparentUnions` is. That keeps a dangling name unrepresentable, and the cost is one
mechanical line in a full record literal.

*Decided: D163 holds by construction.* A seam union declared under `LowerFirst` cannot write a tag that does
not follow its case name, and two cases of one union cannot share one. Two seams still share a tag only by
sharing a case name, which D101 keeps apart. Phase 528's test-level guard stays as the cross-union check.

*Decided: a hosted codec declares its refusal.* `HostedCodec.Refusal` is `Sentence` (the decode answers
`Result<'host, string>` and the generated decoder lifts it to `OutOfRange` at the slot, as before) or `Typed`
(`Result<'host, DecodeError>`, whose code and path are kept and placed under the slot's path). It is written
inside the slot's `hostSurface`, omitted at `sentence`, because it is a fact about the host codec and never
the wire.

*Decided (driver ruling 2026-10-20, superseding the ruling that a slot-level typed codec would carry it):
`ColumnPredicate`'s literal is a CASE-LEVEL host codec.* The premise that a typed hosted codec at one slot
could state the literal was false. The literal is two sibling members, `type` and `value`, and the value is
read at the type its sibling states, over a host case of two fields (`EqualTo of string * Cell`) where the
wire has three members. A slot writes one member. `IdlUnionCase.Hosted` lets a case declare that the members
beside its tag are read and written by a host codec. Its `FSharp` is the host case's payload as a tuple
type, `Encode` writes the members beside the tag, and `Decode` reads the case object under the declared
refusal. The case's `Fields` still state its wire members, and the interpreter, the TypeScript host, the
schema and the F* model read those. A case codec was chosen over a spread construct because the dependent
read is host knowledge, and stating it declaratively would need dependent types the IDL should not grow.
`Declare.errors` refuses a case codec that declares a wire form or format, or sits on a transparent case.
A structural derivation over a vocabulary reaching such a case, and a scaffold or default literal of one,
are refused by name. The classifier reads a case codec's move as undecided (`UnionCaseHostedChanged`), as
it reads a hosted slot's.

*Decided: the codec-only module.* `Gen.fsharpCodecModule sup { Roots; HostTypes } moduleName idl` prints,
for the named unions, records and enums and everything they reach, an abbreviation of each declaration's
host type (`type InvokeError = Fuaran.Core.InvokeError`). It then prints the encoder and decoder groups the
structural module prints, with no type declaration of its own, and per root `encode<Name>`, `decode<Name>`
and `decode<Name>Strict`. Cases are matched and built through the abbreviation, which F# resolves whether or
not the host type requires qualified access; that is how "qualified or unqualified" is answered. It refuses
by name a root the vocabulary does not declare, a reached declaration with no host type, a reached node, and
support that declares types. A generic root's entries take one encoder or decoder per type parameter. The
generator already passed codecs for generic unions (Phase 317), so the generic-payload task's premise, that
`TVar` had no codec, was half true: it holds for the interpreter's lowering and not for the generators. What
was missing was the public entry, and that is what this phase adds.

*Decided: the strict-members reading, as data on the lowered form (the 2026-10-02 bundle's item 1).*
`WireForm.roster` derives the members an object of a declared shape may carry: the layout's own (the
discriminator, a node's `id` and kind key) and every spelling of every wire field. A host-only field is not
on the wire. A strict reading checks each declared object's members against it first, with
`Decoder.members`, and then reads exactly as the lenient reading does. An undeclared member is
`UndeclaredMember` at it, and a document both readings accept decodes to one value. The interpreter answers
it as `Decode.valueStrictDetailed` / `decodeStrictDetailed`, and the codec-only module as
`decode<Name>Strict`. A verbatim, hosted or type-parameter slot is its own reader's to police, as the seams'
strict readers leave a `ready` payload to its decoder. The reading is a separate entry rather than a policy
argument, because `ReadPolicy` lives in `Fuaran.Core.Function` and the IDL does not reference it. Phase 551
wraps the pair at the seam.

*Ruled: the 2026-10-02 bundle's item 2.* This phase is the IDL policy phase item 2 asked for, and it ships
the one policy a consumer needs: strict members. Item bounds, int ranges and admit sets stay undeclared.
No seam and no vocabulary asks for them, and the reuse axis wants a rule-of-three before a new declaration
form. The decode vectors Phase 337 pinned as interpreter-only stay pinned there. A vocabulary that needs one
of the three files it as its own phase.

*Ruled: the TypeScript host gets neither a strict reading nor a codec-only mode.* A TypeScript type is
structural, so there is no host-declared type to abbreviate, and its seam consumers read through the F#
host. The derivation of the nine seam unions is Phase 551.

**AMENDS:** D163 (Status: Amended-by D198. The tag-naming rule now holds by construction: IdlUnion.TagRule = LowerFirst derives each seam case's tag from its name, and Declare refuses two cases of one union with one derived tag). D195 (Status: Amended-by D198. Its "Not decided here" is decided: ColumnPredicate's typed literal is a case-level host codec, not a spread member and not a slot-level typed codec).

## 2026-10-20 — D199: `Fuaran.Core.Text` is the kernel below `Tree`, `Wire` and `OpStream`: one hash, one digest, one escape, one UTF-8 and UTF-16 rule, one string-token grammar and the profiles; the copies go, and the two readers keep their structure and their vocabularies; amends D2 in full

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 531. New package `Fuaran.Core.Text` (`Hash.fs`, `EncodingProfile.fs` and `Xorshift32.fs` moved into it; `JsonString.fs` and `JsonSyntax.fs` new). `Tree`, `Wire` and `OpStream` reference it; `Chain.fs`'s FNV-1a and SHA-256 copies, `Actor.fs`'s escape copy, `Column`'s FNV-1a and canonical-field copies, `Json.fs`'s escape body, frozen `V1` escape, UTF-16 rule, UTF-8 count and string reader, and `Jsonl.fs`'s string, literal and escape scanner bodies are deleted for the kernel's. No hash, escape, digest or JSONL position moves.**

*D2 amended in full (D199.1): standalone over the text kernel.* D2 kept `OpStream` and `Wire` free of every other Core package so an op-stream-only or a wire-only consumer paid for nothing else, and D15, D76, D83, D120, D125 and D158 each read it as forbidding the one thing both needed from below them, so the spine carried value-identical copies held equal by vectors: the FNV-1a chain hash and the SHA-256 digest with its UTF-8 encoder in `OpStream`, the string escape twice (`JsonString` in `OpStream`), the FNV-1a and the canonical field encoding in `Column`, a second strict string and literal grammar in `OpStream.Jsonl`, and the profile carried twice until Phase 516. The ruling (operator, 2026-10-17) is the one this entry records: `Fuaran.Core.Text`, FSharp.Core only and Fable-clean, sits BELOW `Tree`, `Wire` and `OpStream` and carries the hash (`Hash.fnv1a`, `Hash.sha256Hex` and their byte forms), the typed `Digest`, the UTF-8 encoding and the UTF-16 well-formedness rule (`Hash.utf8Bytes`, `Hash.firstIllFormedUnit`, `Hash.utf8ByteCount`), the escape (`JsonString`), the strict lexical grammar (`JsonSyntax`) and the profiles (`EncodingProfile`, `Rendering`). `Tree`, `Wire` and `OpStream` each reference it and nothing else in Core; every other package keeps the references it had. What D2 bought is kept in its terms: an op-stream-only consumer restores `OpStream` and the small kernel, and no `Wire` and no `Tree`; a wire-only consumer restores `Wire` and the kernel. The price is one more package on the roster and one more cohort member in the workspace's cohort file, which is an operator act outside this repository. D125's rule, "a kernel two packages need lives in the lower one", finally has a lower one.

*One string reader, two placements (D199.2).* `JsonSyntax.readString` / `skipString` is the one reader of a JSON string token on the spine: the eight short escapes and `\uXXXX`, no raw control character, well-formed UTF-16 whichever spelling each half arrived in, an optional code-point bound, by runs, and one `Substring` for an escape-free token. It answers a refusal as a value — the rule broken (`JsonStringFault`) and where (`JsonStringRefusal`: the cursor, the start of the unit, and the high surrogate still waiting for its low half with its spelling) — because the two readers built on it have always placed a refusal differently, and both placements are contract: `Json.read` at its cursor with its `JsonErrorKind` and sentence (the cross-host refusal corpus pins them), and the JSONL line reader at the start of what it names with its `JsonlFaultReason` (D158; `proofs/OpStreamLoad.fst`'s `string_tail`; `JsonlDecodeRunTests`). Each reader maps the facts to its own vocabulary in one match. The mapping was derived case by case and is measured, not argued: a differential over 80,000 drawn documents (strings of escapes, raw and escaped surrogate halves in every order, controls, unterminated and truncated tokens, structure around them) reads every one through `Json.read` under three option sets, `Json.parse`, `Jsonl.parseLine`, `checkRaw`, `unquote` and `rawSpan`, and every escape and hash function, on the build before this phase and after it, and the outputs are byte-identical; so is the load of a copy of a live six-lane DAG store (3,184 nodes, one head, SHA-256 verification, every lane re-written to the same bytes). The number grammar is one predicate (`JsonSyntax.isNumber`), which `Json.isJsonNumber` and the line reader's literal check both read; representability (finite, an exact integer past 2^53) stays the document parser's question.

*The structure stays with each reader (D199.3; a premise of the redesign pass checked and found false).* The pass read A §5.1 as "`skipContainer`, `skipValue` and `membersOf` become calls into the scanner's members". They do not, and the reason is structural, not effort: `Json`'s scanner is a recursive descent under a depth cap, read in PULL order by the typed `Reader` (Phase 368), which drives it from a decoder's shape; the line reader is an ITERATIVE walk with no depth cap at all ("no depth of nesting exhausts the call stack", D158), recording raw spans at depth 0 and never materialising a value. Neither can be the other without losing what it is for: the iterative walk cannot serve a pull reader, and the recursive descent would overflow the stack on a line the line reader must refuse by name. Their structural vocabularies differ too (`MissingValue` and `Truncated` against `UnexpectedChar` and `UnexpectedEndOfInput`, at different positions). What they share is the TOKEN grammar — strings, escapes, surrogates, numbers, literals, whitespace — which is where every drift D157 and D158 recorded was, and which is now one body. So "one strict JSON scanner" means one token grammar under two structural walks, each of which is the only walk of its kind.

*`Fable.Core` is not taken (D199.4).* The kernel is FSharp.Core only, as ruled. `Wire`'s escape found its first escapable character under Fable with a native regex (`[<Emit>]`, Phase 365, measured 0.21 ms to 0.12 ms on a long escape-free string under node). That one line was the engineering decision the pass named: a compile-only `Fable.Core` reference on the kernel, or an `Emit` shim kept in `Wire`. Neither is taken. The shim would be a second spelling of the escaped class beside the loop — the drift this package exists to close — and the reference would make the kernel the one FSharp.Core-only package that is not. The loop is the rule on both pipelines; the cost is the measured fraction of a millisecond on long clean strings under node, and the doctrine's durability-over-speed axis decides it. `Wire` keeps its `Fable.Core` reference for `FloatLayout`, unchanged.

*The RNG ends here (D199.5).* `Xorshift32`, moved to `Wire` by Phase 495 as the lowest package drawing from it, moves once more into the kernel, internal, read by `Corpus.genJVal`, the IDL sampler and `ConfRng` through `InternalsVisibleTo`, each from a `NoInlining` function (D129). `Digest`'s bytes-level constructor stays internal, granted to `Tree` and `ContentAddress` as D122 route B granted it from `Tree`.

*Rejected.* (1) A LINKED source file (`<Compile Include="../Fuaran.Core.Wire/JsonSyntax.fs" />` in `OpStream`), which D2 did not forbid and which costs a consumer nothing: it compiles the grammar into two assemblies, so a host holding both carries two copies of every type in it and a fix lands in one package's binary and not the other's until both are re-packed — a copy by another name. (2) Keeping `Json.escape`, `Json.isJsonNumber`, `Json.firstIllFormedUnit` and `Jsonl.quote` out of the public surface: they are the names consumers in every tier call, and each is now one line over the kernel, not a body. (3) A third, typed lexical-event scanner both readers consume: it would move the structure decision into the kernel without removing either walk.

**AMENDS:** D2 (amended in full; Status → `Amended-by D199`), and marks the copy justifications superseded in D15 (`Amended-by D199` — the digest's home is the kernel; the default chain hash is unchanged), D76 (`Amended-by D199` — the standalone packages carry the escape as a reference, not a pinned copy), D83 (`Amended-by D187, D199` — the scanner's token grammar is the kernel's), D120 (`Amended-by D188, D199` — the profile is carried once, in the kernel), D125 (`Amended-by D194, D199` — the lower package exists: the RNG and the digest constructor live in it) and D158 (`Amended-by D199` — the line reader shares D157's code for its token grammar, not only its vectors).

## 2026-10-20 — D197: `DagFold` is two modules, one proof style each; `fold_confluence` and the second `mergeBase` model are retired, and every theorem about `Dag.mergeBase` is stated over the function that runs

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 534. `proofs/DagFold.fst`, `proofs/DagClosure.fst` (new), `proofs/DagPrimitives.fst`, `proofs/Skeleton.fst`, `proofs/kit/templates/Instance.fst.template`, the two extracted oracles, `proofs.json`, `proofs/modules.json`, `copies.json`. No production code and no package surface changed.**

*The split (D197.1; amends D156).* `DagFold.fst` was 6,584 lines in one module written in two proof styles: sections 0–10, the fold over lane deltas already known, are a small algebra whose list facts carry SMT patterns; sections 11–21, the DAG beneath the fold, carry none and call every lemma by name. They are now two modules: `DagFold` (sections 0–10, about 1,000 lines) and `DagClosure` (sections 11–21, about 5,600 lines), which opens it. The section numbers are kept, so every citation of "section 13" or "13.13" still lands. D156 declined to split `Temporal` and `OpStreamLoad`, and it was right about them: their cost sat in a handful of queries whose context carried definitions the proof never needed, and naming what each query may use cut it where a split would have moved nothing. `DagFold` differs in kind, not degree: its cost is spread across two bodies of proof with two disciplines, and a lemma added to one half was checked in the context of the other. Measured by D156's method (cold, direct invocation at the leg's flags, dependencies in the cache, no other prover on the machine): `DagFold` 11s to 12s and `DagClosure` 40s to 59s over four cold runs each (`DagPrimitives` 11s to 15s), against the one module's 117s to 178s; each has its own budget in `modules.json`. The pure list helpers the tree models open `DagFold` for (`rev_app`, `rev_rev`, `mem_rev`, `keep` with `mem_keep` and `keep_ext`) moved into its section 0, so `TreeDiff`, `Normalize`, `TreeFrame` and every tree model still open `DagFold` alone, see the context they saw, and never wait on `DagClosure`; the shard's expected re-pointing of `Arbitrate` and `Normalize` opens was therefore not needed. The context is the point, not only the names: the split's first cold run left `mem_rev`, whose SMT pattern fires on `mem x (rev l)`, in `DagClosure`, and `TreeFrame.chain_has_target`, which never names it, stopped verifying. A pattern is part of what a module exports.

*Section 12 dissolved, its theorems kept (D197.2).* The ruling deleted section 12, the spine case Phase 142 proved, keeping 13.12's corollary names. Deleting its theorems would have narrowed the `topological-order-choice` row: its spine results hold at EVERY selector, and 13.12's corollaries only at `pick_min`. The ruling's goal was one coherent module tree, not a weaker ladder, so section 12 is dissolved as a section and nothing it proved is lost: its definitions (the frontier drain at every selector) are 13.0, which the rest of section 13 is built on, and its theorems are 13.12.1–13.12.5, beside the corollaries that re-derive them at the id order (13.12.6).

*`fold_confluence` retired (D197.3).* It was `fold_confluence_total` with the Phase 131 `lanes_apply` premise kept, and stayed only because `Skeleton.fst` and the instantiation template called it. Both are discharged by `fold_confluence_total` now, and so is `fold_confluence_dag`. The instance statements keep `lanes_apply` in their `requires`, unused by the proof: dropping it would change a theorem statement, which this phase does not do. The `fold-confluence` row is retired with a note in `proofs/README.md`; `fold-confluence-total` and `fold_confluence_halt` carry everything it said.

*One model of `Dag.mergeBase`, production's (D197.4).* Phase 158 modelled `mergeBase` as it then ran — the maximum by (closure size, id) over the whole common set — and Phase 388 changed production to `deepest`, which sizes only the maximal members when the common set drains completely. Phase 457 modelled `deepest` (`merge_base_now`) and proved it equal to the old model over a witnessed closure, so two models stood, with theorems about the old one carried across by that equality. The old model is deleted. THEOREM 5 is `DagPrimitives.merge_base_now_maximal`, standing on `DagClosure.max_common_is_maximal` and `deepest_is_max_by`; the `merge-base-maximal` row is retired into `merge-base-as-it-runs`, which carries its whole claim (any two heads, a criss-cross included, the refusal over disjoint histories, the tie-break left as policy). The divergence theorem is restated over the function that runs, `merge_base_now_is_divergence(_acyclic)`, with the same premises and for every `lt` and every drain fuel: every common member but `m` lies below a parent of `m`, which is itself a member, so `deepest`'s filter keeps `m` alone or nothing, and either branch of the drain test answers `m`. No new premise and no weaker conclusion. The `merge-base-divergence` row is re-pointed at it, and its sentence that `merge_base` "is production's function clause for clause", false since Phase 388, is corrected. The bridge `merge_base_now_is_merge_base` is deleted with the model it bridged to.

*Rejected.* (1) Section 17 (slot writes commute) into `DagFold`: its subject is footprints, but the ruling divides by proof style and section 17 is written in `DagClosure`'s; moving it would make the module boundary a judgement per section rather than a rule. (2) The four list helpers into `ListAlgebra`, their natural home: that module is copied by every adopter and is not this phase's to grow; `DagFold` section 0 keeps them one hop from where they were. (3) A `{{FOLD}}_confluence_total` instance theorem with no `requires`: a new statement, left for a phase that decides it.

## 2026-10-20 — D196: `fuaran-core-idl` refuses on one channel, and `support.json` is read on the decode layer

**Status:** Live

Phase 526. The IDL tool carried two strict argument parsers and two refusal channels: `classify` refused on stdout, `spike-proposal` (moved in from the test runner at Phase 230 with its own parser) on stderr. It now has ONE verb table - each verb's positionals and flags are data, one parser reads them (a flag given twice is refused), the usage is rendered from the table, and every outcome reaches the exit code through one map, so no exit code moved. The refusal channel is stdout, `fuaran-core-idl: <sentence>`, exit 2, for every verb: stdout already carried every report and `classify`'s refusals, a downstream generation step then reads one refusal shape whichever verb failed, and nothing consumed the stderr stream. The alternative - keep stderr for the spike and document it - was rejected because it keeps two shapes for one contract. `ProposalSpike`'s `ExternalLeg` seam is removed rather than populated: populating it (a `--ts-runner` flag) would have an FSharp.Core-only tool spawn a JavaScript runtime and transpile TypeScript for a cross-host agreement the repository's own suites already measure; the spike's `generate` leg instead runs every backend the generator has, the F* model over the touched kinds `FStarTarget.partition` admits. `SupportArtifact` reads through a `Decoder` (S7), so its refusals carry a `DecodeCode` and a path as `idl.json`'s do; the writer is untouched and `support.json` bytes do not move. It stays a decoder rather than a full `Codec`: the bytes are the contract and the reader was the defect. `docs/idl-stability-classes.md`'s usage block is the command's `--help`, held byte-equal by a test.

## 2026-10-20 — D195: the seams' refusal unions stay hand-declared public types; their codecs are derived by a codec-only generator mode, after the IDL gains the five features the derivation needs

**Status:** Amended-by D198, D200

**Recorded by Phase 528 (a premise refutation); the ruling is the operator's.**

*Found.* Phase 528 was filed on the premise that the IDL already carried what a derivation of the seams' refusal codecs needs. The phase measured the opposite. The IDL has no tag-naming rule: a union case's tag is both the host case name and the wire tag. Its generator emits codecs only for types it also emits. A hosted slot's refusal is lifted to `OutOfRange` at the slot, losing the hosted codec's own code and path. A type parameter has no wire form. Nothing in it states a strict-members policy. Deriving the codecs without those features would move pinned refusal codes and paths, which the seams' documents and journals forbid.

*Decided (operator ruling).* `InvokeError`, `QueryError`, `DeclarationFault`, `Placement`, `Deferred`, `ColumnPredicate` / `SortKey`, `ArgSource` / `PipelineNode`, `FieldChange` and `Rejection` stay HAND-DECLARED public types in their own namespaces and modules: a stable surface, documented where it is declared, with the unqualified case names every consumer matches on. The generator gains a CODEC-ONLY mode that derives the codecs, and the strict rosters beside them, for types it does not emit. The alternative, moving the public types into generated modules, is rejected because it would move every consumer's pattern match to buy what a codec-only mode buys without it.

*Sequenced.* The IDL prerequisites go to fuaran-core#550: the tag-naming rule on `UnionForm`'s case tags (D163's "the tag follows the case name"), the codec-only mode, typed hosted decoders that keep a hosted codec's code and path, codecs for type parameters taking a payload codec, and a strict-members policy. The derivation itself (the nine unions declared, the hand codecs deleted, `decodeErrorOf` moved to Wire, the strict rosters derived) goes to fuaran-core#551, which depends on fuaran-core#550. Until then the seams' bytes, reader refusals and journals are pinned by `FunctionTests.seamBaselineTests528` and `QueryTests.seamBaselineTests528`. The same test holds D163 over the refusal unions: every tag is its case name lowered, every case is pinned, and no two refusal unions share a tag.

*Not decided here.* Whether `ColumnPredicate`'s typed literal (one cell written as `type` and `value`) is stated in the IDL as a spread member or stays a typed hosted codec is fuaran-core#550's to rule on. Both keep the bytes, but they differ in what a non-F# host can derive.

## 2026-10-20 — D194: the generator's published types live in `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen.Types`, so a public module splits one concern per file; the classifier is one rule over a typed snapshot; a member's value is one presence rule; every codec, literal, value and derivation question is one traversal under a printer per backend

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 524. `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen`; rides the `0.40.0` slot (STABILITY.md, "The generated layer is printed from ONE resolution"). Amends D125.**

*Decided (operator ruling 2026-10-17, D125 amended): lifting is the rule when a public module's nested types are what keep it in one file.* D125 recorded that `Diff` and `FStarTarget` could not split without renaming their nested types in the `api/` baseline. It held the split until a surface move with a reason of its own, and the 1.0 retype is that reason. The public types of `Gen` (`GenSupport`, `KindProjection`, `Derivation`), `FStarTarget` (`Provenance`, `VectorModel`, and `KindVerdict`, the renamed `FStarTarget.Verdict`) and `Diff` (the snapshot types, `Change`, `Severity`, `Classification`, `FSharpConsequence`, `Verdict`, `VerdictClass`, `Bump`, `HostRole`, `Host`, `Strength`, `Obligation`) are declared in `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen.Types`, ahead of every emitter. `FStar.fs` becomes four internal modules behind the `FStarTarget` facade, and `Diff.fs` six behind the `Diff` facade. `FStarTarget.Slot`, public by accident, is internal. The mirrors D96 recorded (`Core.Projection`, `Core.Support`, `FSharpDerive.Request` and their converters) are deleted. The collecting decoders are a member of the one request set (`Derivation.SpecDecoders`). `SourceLengthTests`' exception list loses `Diff.fs` and `FStar.fs`, while `DagOpStream.fs` remains for the reason D125 gives.

*Decided: the stability classifier decides on types, through one rule.* A field is read once into `FieldSnap`, holding a `WireType`, a `HostSurface` and a `PresenceSnap`; before, it was eight canonical strings that three rules parsed back into JSON. `ruleOf : Change -> Rule` is one total match of 36 arms in rank order. It replaces 36 closure rows that reflection joined to the union, and their 108 unreachable `misapplied` arms. `classify`, `consequences`, `sortKey`, `summarise`, the family predicates and `mappingTable` are projections of it, and the table enumerates `DiffRules.exemplars`, which `IdlDiffTests` holds to the union. `verdict` is computed once, and `report` and `verdictBlock` render it. The twelve doors are four: `parse`, `ofArtifacts`, `ofValues` and `run`.

*Decided: a member's value is one rule, `Decl.memberValue` (carried 511.t4).* The rule takes the site (`Literal`, `Constructor` or `Scaffold`), the declared optionality and the offered value, and answers a `MemberValue`. The two policies the sites differed in are stated there once:

- A host-only member is refused inside a literal and takes its placeholder elsewhere.
- A required member with no value is the caller's parameter at a constructor and refused elsewhere.

Every backend prints the answer and decides nothing.

*Decided (B §8 S10): every question the F# and TypeScript emitters both answer is one traversal, and each backend contributes a printer record.* The traversals are in `Emit/Printer.fs`, and the derivations' plans in `Emit/DeriveTraversal.fs` (`Derive`).

- `SlotTraversal.slotFn` reads every slot's encoder, decoder and collecting decoder over one `SlotPrinter` type. The collecting printer is derived from the decoder's, so a leaf's collecting form is its decoder lifted by construction.
- `MemberEncTraversal` reads a member under its presence (a typed `MemberPiece`), and `MemberTraversal` reads it back short-circuiting or collecting.
- `UnionEncTraversal` and `UnionTraversal` read a union's cases and its transparent case. A declared transparent tag naming no case is refused by both hosts, as the TypeScript backend always refused it.
- `CollectingTraversal` reads the collecting group in its one order.
- `LiteralTraversal` prints a declared literal over `Decl.literal`. The F# literal and the TypeScript omit test are its printers, so the two backends admit one set of defaults by construction.
- `ValueTraversal` prints an authored value.
- `Derive` plans the structural derivations: structural positions and their child layout, the keyed plan and its position walk, slot positions, the fold plan and walk, projection carriers, the requested union modules, default records and constants.

The enum decoders share no decision and stay each backend's own. The generated runtime preludes are template files (`Templates/`, embedded and read by `Template.text`), copied unchanged. This removed every duplicated walk; one generated line moved. The F# scaffold of a node authored without an envelope now fills the envelope's members, as the TypeScript scaffold did; the old record literal did not compile.

*Decided: two uncalled members and one vocabulary's residue are removed.* `Diff.declaredRoster` and `Trust.hardenOrRefuse` are removed: they had no caller outside this repository's tests. The F# module no longer writes `encodeStateBehaviourJson` / `encodeSemanticStyleJson` (C93); a vocabulary that wants them declares them through its accessor splice. Prepending the two lines to the UI vocabulary's splice reproduces its generated module byte for byte (measured).

## 2026-10-20 — D193: `idl.json` is one `Codec<Idl>` (write, strict collecting read and schema from one declaration, the omit rule one table), a proposal is read by it under an admission policy, and no description is written for a vocabulary that declares none; D122 gains its first in-repo consumer and D51's question is closed

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 527. `Fuaran.Core.Idl` (`Artifact`, `Proposal`) and `Fuaran.Core.Wire` (`Codec`); rides the `0.40.0` slot (breaking).**

*Decided: the artifact is a codec.* `Artifact.codec : Codec<Idl>` (and `codecWith identity`) is built from `Wire`'s `Codec.record` / `field` / `optField` / `union`. The writer, the reader and the schema cannot disagree about a member. Each of the six conditional-emission clauses, with its hand-written reader mirror, is one `Codec.defaultField` / `optField` declaration. The omit-at-default rules are one table of typed rows (`Artifact.omitted`), each used once by the codec. The schema is the codec's, hoisted to a 2020-12 document (`Artifact.schema`, committed at `conformance/idl/idl.schema.json` with a stamp in `$comment`). `parse (render idl) = canonicalise idl` is unchanged. Both published `idl.json` artifacts re-render byte for byte under their own identity, and both validate against the schema.

*Decided: the read is strict and collects.* An undeclared member is `UndeclaredMember`, where the hand readers dropped it silently. That is the encoding-version argument applied to every member: a reader that drops what it does not know thins a vocabulary quietly. The encoding version is still checked first and refused alone. Every other defect is answered, each at its path, then every `Declare.errors` fault at its owner's path. Members the old reader read leniently when absent (`args`, `params`, `harden`, a sentinel's `wire`) are always written and still read leniently. A sentinel that is present is checked against its fixed spelling. `transparentCase` stays derived: written, then read and discarded.

*Decided: one reader of the encoding, the refusals kept.* `Proposal` reads types, defaults, optionalities and annotations through `Artifact`'s codecs, then admits as a policy: a host-surface type, a host-only slot, a non-scalar default or a non-doc annotation is `NotAdmitted` at its own path, raised by walking the path (D151's shape). The argument that the two readers had to stay separate held only for a reader with no policy parameter, and it is deleted with them. A proposal may carry the doc of a member it mints.

*Decided (D40 amended, ruling 1A of 2026-10-17): no default description.* `Artifact.Identity` is two optional members. `render` declares neither, so a vocabulary that declares no description gets none, where every nameless artifact used to carry the UI vocabulary's prose. `defaultDescription` and `defaultIdentity` are removed, and `unnamed` replaces the latter. Two consequences, both deliberate. (1) The UI tier's `idl.json` re-renders without its description line unless that tier declares its prose through `renderWith`. (2) `Stamp.vocabulary` hashes `Artifact.json`, so every generated artefact's `vocabulary` stamp line moves once.

*Noted (D122, ruling A of 2026-10-17): `Codec<'T>` stays on the spine.* `Artifact.codec` is its first in-repository production consumer, which is the evidence D51's membership rule asked for, and D51's open question is closed on the record. The kit grew the five combinators the consumer needed and nothing more: `defaultField`, `entries`, `narrow` (a refinement whose refusals walk their paths), `recursive` (a self-referential codec with one `$defs` definition) and `schemaDocument` (the standalone schema, its definitions hoisted).

*Rejected.* (1) Widening `Idl` with an identity, which breaks every vocabulary built by literal. (2) A tolerant codec build mode, because strictness with a version gate is the posture the version comment already argued for. (3) Reading `transparentCase` back as a cross-check, which would refuse an artifact rendered before Phase 179.

## 2026-10-20 — D192: every DAG write answers one `Written` record, the DAG folds once over one drain, a cyclic history is one `Cyclic`, and no `OpStream.Dag` answer carries a tuple; the writes take the one `Stream`; amends D140 (complete) and D189

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 529. `Fuaran.Core.OpStream.Dag`'s `api/` baseline, `OneDotZeroTests`' pair rule, the `0.40.0` slot.**

*The record (D192.1).* `Dag.Written<'Op> = { Id; Dag }` is the node a write recorded and the DAG holding it. `appendOn`, `append`, `merge` and `mergeAll` answer it; `mergeWith` answers one per node it recorded (`[]` for an empty script); `CheckedAppend { State; Written }`, `IndexedAppend { Written; Reach }` and `LaneAppend { Written; Loaded }` carry it as their `Written` field. Considered and rejected: one record with `State: 'State option` and `Reach: Reach option` (the redesign pass's C112) - option-as-mode, which D138.1 bars on a frozen surface, and a checked caller would unwrap a `Some` it knows is there; and collapsing the fifteen verbs to four - a rename of every consumer call site for no new capability.

*The stream (D192.2).* Every write and the verifying loads (`fromJsonlVerified`, `loadLanesVerified`, `verifyLanes`) take the one `Stream` (D189) and mint or verify through `nodeId s`. Under `StreamConfig.canonical` every id is the one `0.39.0` minted; a store kept under a legacy profile is now written and verified under its own spelling. The checkpoint verbs keep `hashFn`/`w` for now: their seal is the `Sealed`/`Anchor` surface (D187).

*One fold, one drain, one cycle (D192.3).* One private `fold` replaces the six replay loops; `Reach.ofDag` is `drainNodes` plus the bitset pass; the head drain is `drainClosure`. `Dag.Cyclic { Unplaced }` - every node a drain left, in id order - is the one cyclic answer: `tryTopoOrder` (a sentence before), `totalOrderBy`/`ranks`/`totalOrder` (`TotalOrderFault` removed), `ReplayFault.Cyclic` (was `CyclicHistory` of the head or the first cyclic root, found by a second drain per root), `ReplayAllFault.Cyclic`, `RehashFault.Cyclic`. The F* models are unchanged; the differential reads production's `Cyclic` as the model's head when the head is among the unplaced nodes.

*Typed refusals (D192.4, D99/D146 applied).* `prunable` refuses `PruneFault.UnknownRoot`; `tryLanesToJsonl` refuses a `LaneWriteFault { Lane; Fault }`; a checkpoint sidecar line is refused by four `JsonlFaultReason` cases (`CheckpointNotAtSeqZero`, `CheckpointWithoutNode`, `CheckpointChainOnly`, `NotACheckpoint`) rendering the sentences they replace.

*The rule's reach (D192.5, completes D140).* Over `Fuaran.Core.OpStream.Dag` no public function answers a tuple of ANY width; the other packages keep D140.5's three-or-more rule. The DAG's remaining pairs became records named for what they hold: `Compaction`, `CheckpointedText`, `Checkpointed`, `LaneText` (which `loadLanes` also takes), `LaneCollision`, `DisjointRoot`, `Rehashed`, `RehashedLanes`.

**Consequences.** `Fuaran.Core.OpStream.Dag` moves by removal and retype, `Fuaran.Core.OpStream` by union-widening, paid by `0.40.0`. No content id, lane byte, total order, fold verdict, wire baseline or corpus byte moves; a live lane store and synthetic DAGs were pinned old against new. `Reach.ofDag` costs about 3 ms more per build at 3,115 nodes for sharing the drain; `mergeBase` is unchanged.

## 2026-10-20 — D191: the UI corpus's chain, DAG, merge and diff families stay UI-produced, because every vector in them carries bytes only a UI-tier codec writes; Core's share of them is already Core-owned as the escape, encoding and apply families

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 479**, which was chartered to move the production of the shared corpus's `chain/`,
`dag/`, `merge-conformance/` and `diff/` families from the UI hosts to this repository, on the premise
that "their semantics are Core's", with the corpus keeping a fingerprint-checked copy declared in
`copies.json`. Its acceptance bar was a Core export reproducing each corpus file byte for byte, and any
difference was to be recorded before anything moved. Nothing moves. The premise is false for all four
families, and this entry is the finding.

*The inventory (D191.1).* Read against the corpus at `1594c42` and `fuaran-dotnet` at `47049ed`. Each
family is a mechanism this package owns, instantiated over the UI tier's domain payload:

| Corpus family | Vectors | Producer today | Core's part | The UI tier's part, in every vector |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` (`chain-corpus.json`) | 3 records | the F# host's `HashChain.computeHash`; no producer record, the directory having no manifest (so `corpus-producers.json` lists no family for it); asserted by `fuaran-dotnet` and the TypeScript host | `OpStream.canonicalConfig.Payload` and the SHA-256 hash | the payload's bytes: `StreamEntry.encode`, the `{"v":2,"op",…,"result"}` envelope over a `TreeOp` read from the corpus's own `ops/` family, and an `OpResultEnvelope` |
| `dag` | 4 round-trip records | `fuaran-dotnet` `--emit-dag-corpus` (`DagCorpus.fs`) | `Dag.nodeId`'s content-address discipline | the record's `op` (a `TreeOp`, `$type` `RemoveNode` / `Batch`), `resultEnvelope` (`$type` `Success`) and the record codec, all inside the address pre-image |
| `merge-conformance` | 13 fixtures (4 `merge-3way` / `merge-validator-gated`, 3 refusal, 6 totality) | `fuaran-dotnet` `--emit-merge-corpus` (`MergeCorpus.fs`) | `Dag.merge` / `Dag.reconcile` and the conflict shapes | UI trees (`Box`, `Markdown`, `Auto` layout, accessibility roles), the `SemanticStyle` sub-field blend, and a sample DOMAIN validator's verdict |
| `diff` (`goldens.json`) | 10 goldens, 3 divergent | `authored`: scripts generated by the go, rs and py producers, per host where they diverge | the `Diff` module's structural passes | UI node kinds, and ops `SkeletonOp` does not have: `PatchStyle`, `UpdateStyle`, `UpdateProp`, `EditNode`, `ReplaceRoot` |

*Why no Core export can reproduce them (D191.2).* This package owns no node type (the `apply/` family's
exporter header, D37), and the spine takes no dependency on the UI tier above it. A Core render of any of
these files would have to restate the UI tier's `TreeOp`, node, style and result codecs inside this
repository's tests: a second implementation of another tier's contract, which would drift from the one the UI hosts
ship the first time either moved, and would certify nothing a UI host does not already certify. The `0.33.0`
release record already said as much of the chain corpus ("It cannot be emitted from here"), and this
entry extends it to the other three. The falsifier is a vector in one of the four families whose bytes
this package can produce from its own types. There is none today: every one embeds a `$type`-tagged UI
value, and the chain records hash one.

*What a UI-free Core port certifies against instead (D191.3).* The part of those families that IS
Core's is already pinned as Core-owned vectors: `escape/string-escape.json` (the linear chain pre-image
at sequence 0 for each actor), `encoding/encoding-profiles.json` (an actor's encoding as folded into a
chain payload and a DAG node id, under each profile), and `apply/skeleton-apply.json` (the skeleton op
contract over a witness with no domain payload). A family that certifies a port's chain WALK, DAG fold,
merge or skeleton diff end to end, over the skeleton witness, does not exist yet. It is new design:
which witness, which payload shape, which corpus paths. It is not a move, so it is left to its own
phase and not built here.

*What the UI side keeps (D191.4).* The four families stay produced by the UI hosts, which is what
`corpus-producers.json` already records (for `chain`, which has no record, what its description says). They certify the UI tier's binding of Core's mechanisms, which
is a UI contract. No `copies.json` record is added, because there is no Core-emitted file to copy. A
fuaran-side phase that names `fuaran-core#479` as the place where `diff/`'s producer moves should drop
that clause. The `diff` row's remaining question, whether the F# reference emits it or it stays
authored, is the UI side's to decide.

## 2026-10-20 — D190: the IDL declares a member's aliases, an enum case's aliases and a member's presence condition, and admits an empty-map and a JSON default in every backend; decode accepts and normalises, encode writes the canonical form, the sampler draws it

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 539.** `src/Fuaran.Core.Idl/` (`Idl.fs`, `WireForm.fs`, `Declare.fs`, `Encode.fs`,
`Decode.fs`, `Sample.fs`, `Artifact.fs`, `Proposal.fs`), `src/Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen/` (`Emit/Decl.fs`,
`Emit/FSharpDefaults.fs`, `Emit/FSharpCanonicalForm.fs`, `Emit/FSharpCodec.fs`, `Emit/TypeScriptCodec.fs`,
`FStar.fs`, `Gen.fs`, `Diff.fs`), the law set `conformance/laws/canonical-form-laws.json`. rides the `0.40.0` draft
(docs/releases/0.40.0.md, Breaking for F# consumers, additive on the wire). The three canonical-form
rules a UI vocabulary states in its specification (fuaran#2300) could carry only the first, the declared
default, as IDL data; this entry gives the other two, and one literal form, a slot in the contract every
backend reads.

*The currency check (D190.0).* Read against fuaran#2300's held branch and Phase 513's `WireForm` as
landed: the field model had no slot for a presence condition or an alias list (its STABILITY entry and
WIRE_FORMAT §13 both say so), and none has landed since. The third gap was narrower than the shard
said: the interpreter, the validator and the artifact already admitted an `OmitDefault (VMap [])` and an
`OmitDefault (VJson _)`; the code generator's one admissibility (`Decl.literal`) refused both, so no
generated host could honour one. None of the three is struck.

*Decided: aliases (D190.1).* `IdlField.Aliases: string list` — a member's retired spellings, in priority
order — and `IdlEnum.Aliases: (string * string list) list` — the lenient wire strings of a case, keyed by
host case name and sparse, as `CaseAnnotations` is. An alias is DECODE-ONLY: a decoder reads a member under
its canonical name first and then each alias in order, so the canonical spelling wins when both are present
and otherwise the first alias present is the member; an enum alias decodes to its case. Every encoder
writes the canonical spelling, so `decode >> encode` normalises. A refusal inside an aliased member is at
its CANONICAL spelling, in the interpreter and in the generated decoders alike: the decoder normalises,
then reads. In `idl.json` a field carries `"aliases": [...]` and an enum `"aliases": {"<wire>": [...]}`,
each omitted when empty. `Declare.errors` refuses an alias that is not an identifier, that is another
spelling of a member of the same owner, or that is a member every JavaScript object carries; an enum alias
that is empty or multi-line, that is one of the enum's wire strings or another alias, or that names a case
the enum does not declare.

*Decided: presence (D190.2).* `IdlField.Presence: PresenceCondition option`, one of `WhenPresent s`,
`WhenAbsent s` (an `Optional` sibling `s`) and `WhenEquals (s, v)` (a sibling holding the scalar `v` — a
string, an int, a bool or an enum's canonical wire string; an absent `OmitDefault` sibling holds its
default). A member whose condition fails carries no meaning, so it is ABSENT from the canonical form: the
encoder omits it whatever it holds, the decoder accepts it and drops it — so it decodes as its
optionality's absence, `None` or the default — and the sampler draws it absent. Admitted only on an
`Optional` or `OmitDefault` member (only those say what absence means), over a declared, wire-visible,
unconditional sibling that is not the member itself; chains are not admitted. The decoder evaluates the
condition over the RAW object (the sibling read under its own aliases), which is what the generated F#
decoder renders (`dMember` / `dPick`), so the two readings agree by construction. In `idl.json` a field
carries `"presence": {"$type": "whenPresent" | "whenAbsent" | "whenEquals", "sibling": …, "value"?: …}`.
A tag test (a sibling union holding a given case — `Disclosure.defaultOpen` under a bound `open`) is not
admitted: the one row that wants it is already canonical by its declared default, and a fourth test waits
for a second use.

*Decided: map and JSON defaults (D190.3).* `Decl.literal` admits the EMPTY map at a `TMap` slot and a
JSON value at a `TJson` slot whose strings are well-formed and whose numbers are finite. The F# backend
spells them `Map.empty` and the `JVal` constructor expression and tests them with `Map.isEmpty` and by
canonical bytes (`Canonical.write Rendering.CrossHost`), as the interpreter compares them; the TypeScript
backend with `Object.keys(x).length === 0` and `encJson`; the F* model as the empty association list and
a `jval` term, refusing a JSON default holding a number as the opaque numeric boundary it already states.
Nested in a record or union-case default neither has a pattern spelling, so every backend refuses it there
(the D33 agreement rule, held by the Phase 125 property).

*Decided: every backend applies or refuses (D190.4).* The interpreter (`Encode`, `Decode`, `Sample`) and
the generated F# codec, short-circuiting and collecting, apply all three. The TypeScript codec reads each
member under its one name, so `Gen.typescriptModule` and `typescriptModuleDerived` refuse a vocabulary
declaring an alias or a presence condition, naming the first (`UnsupportedConstruct`); the F* model refuses
the same set by name. The TypeScript declarations are unaffected (neither shape moves a type), and the JSON
Schema describes the canonical form: it already requires no conditional member, is open to other members,
and lists an enum's canonical strings only. The stability classifier grades an alias added `additive`, one
withdrawn `breaking-wire`, and a presence condition that appears, moves or vanishes `breaking-wire`
(`FieldAliasesChanged`, `EnumCaseAliasesChanged`, `FieldPresenceChanged`).

*Decided: the laws are vectors (D190.5).* `laws/canonical-form-laws.json` carries the fixture vocabulary's
`idl.json` and, per vector, a document and the canonical bytes the reference reads it to: an alias decodes
to its canonical value and re-encodes canonically, a conditionally-present member is absent exactly when
its condition fails, and a map or JSON default is omitted at its default. It is emitted beside the other
law sets and is not yet a row of the corpus `laws/manifest.json`: the corpus indexes it in the change-set
that first carries the file, the UI tier's cohort raise onto the release carrying this entry, which is
where fuaran#2300's rules 2 and 3 become data.

## 2026-10-20 — D189: an op stream is one `Stream` value and each chain verb exists once; the encoding profiles are `StreamConfig` constructors; the forwarding facade is deleted and each concern file is its public module; amends D58 and D141

**Status:** Amended-by D192

**Recorded by Phase 516.** `src/Fuaran.Core.OpStream/` (every file; `OpStream.fs` deleted),
`src/Fuaran.Core.OpStream.Dag/DagOpStream.fs`, `src/Fuaran.Core.Conformance/` (the three stream law
families, `StoredIdentity`, `EncodingProfileVectors`, `Families`, `Conformance`); rides the `0.39.0` draft
(docs/releases/0.39.0.md, Breaking). No seal, chain hash, node id, checkpoint, JSONL line or refusal
position moved: a pin harness run over the old and new builds wrote the same bytes, the live store
verified under both, and `conformance/` is untouched. Redesign pass C §5.6, §8 slices 8 and 11; the
operator's rulings of 2026-10-17 on D58 and D141 (both A).

*Decided: one value (D189.1).* `Stream<'Op,'State,'Rej>` is `{ Config; HashFn; Witness }`, built by
`OpStream.canonical hashFn w` or `OpStream.ofConfig cfg hashFn w`. Every verb that took the three takes
it once: `OpStream.append` / `appendMany` / `appendChainOnly` / `appendIf` / `appendIdempotent` /
`appendIdempotentIf` / `firstChainBreak` / `verifyChain`, `Jsonl.readVerified`, `Snapshots.take` /
`compact` / `firstBreak` / `verify`, `Compacted.compactAt` / `compactFrom` / `appendTo` / `appendIfTo` /
