`appendIdempotentTo` / `verify`, and the DAG's identity verbs `Dag.nodeId` / `firstBreak` / `verifyDag`.
The `…With cfg` twin of each is the verb, so a stream cannot be appended under one config and verified,
compacted or attested under another. A verb that read less takes what it reads, so the rule is
"what the verb reads", never a phantom witness: `OpStream.head` and the attestation verbs take the
`StreamConfig` (only its genesis is read), the capture journals take the config and the hash (they have
no witness), and `OpStream.replay` / `replayLenient` and every `Snapshots` / `Compacted` replay take the
witness. `appendChainOnly`, `appendIdempotent` and `appendIdempotentIf` were canonical-only and now
honour the stream's config, closing three half-applied configs.

*Decided: one rehash (D189.2).* `OpStream.rehash from into records` verifies under one stream and
re-mints under another, so the payload migration (`tryRehash`), its string-rendered twin (`rehash`) and
the two-witness profile migration (`rehashEncoding`) are one verb; the two streams may differ in config,
hash or witness. `ChainShape.rehash` takes a hash per side so that one verb is the one walk, and the
facade's own rehash loop is gone. `Dag.rehash from into` replaces `rehashWith` (two hashes) and
`rehashEncoding` (two profiles), and `EffectCapture.rehashCaptures fromCfg toCfg` replaces
`rehashCapturesEncoding`, the facade's second loop and its copy of the capture payload. A host that keys
by hash maps old to new by position; the DAG's rehash keeps its id map because a DAG's order is not a
list's.

*Decided: the profiles are constructors (D189.3).* `StreamConfig` gains `Quote` — the spelling of the
strings this package spells inside a pre-image it builds itself (the actor in a DAG node id, a capture's
tags) — and `StreamConfig.canonical` (`V2`), `StreamConfig.legacyEscape` (`V1`) and
`StreamConfig.legacyActor` (pre-Phase-320) are the configs a store declares. `StreamConfig.spellActor`
is the actor's pre-image under a config. `OpStream.EncodingProfile`, `currentProfile`, `profiles`,
`profileName`, `tryProfile`, `encodeActorWith` and `configFor` — the stated mirror of `Wire`'s type that
D120 carried "twice because D2 forbids once" — are removed: a consumer holding both packages maps
`Wire`'s `EncodingProfile` to a config in a two-case match (`StoredIdentity` and `EncodingProfileVectors`
do), and Phase 531's kernel is where one type can serve both. The `EncodingProfileVectors.laws`
outcomes that held the twin's names equal to `Wire`'s go with the twin.

*Decided: the facade goes, and each concern file is its public module (D189.4).* `OpStream.fs`'s 117
forwards are deleted. The chain verbs are `OpStream` (Chain.fs); the scanner, the field readers, the
checked writer and the op stream's record writer and readers are `Jsonl` (`write`, `tryWrite`, `read`,
`readWithSnapshots`, `readLegacyActor`, `readVerified`); the snapshot family is `Snapshots`; the
compacted stream `Compacted`; the positional capture journal `EffectCapture` (its JSONL `toJsonl` /
`tryToJsonl` / `ofJsonl`, the last answering `JsonlFault` as `KeyedCapture.ofJsonl` does); the keyed
journal's verbs join `KeyedCapture`; attestation is `Attestation`; the attributed lift `Attributed`.
Each member keeps its name where its path changed, so a migration is a path rename plus the collapsed
signature. The internal modules that held the bodies are gone with the forwards.

*Decided: the DAG's capability twins stay (D189.5).* Of the twenty-two pairs the pass counted, the
DAG's `tryReplayToWith`, `reconcileManyWith` and `replayFromWith` (over a `Reach` index),
`appendVerifiedWith` and `mergeVerifiedWith` (over a state equality) and `mergeWith` (not a twin) take a
capability, not a config, so a `Stream` does not collapse them; they keep their names, as D170 lets a
`With` name a pinned parameter. The DAG's write and load verbs keep `hashFn w` and mint and verify
under the canonical config; Phase 529 owns the DAG's write surface.

*Decided: the three obsolete forwards are removed (D189.6).* `Conformance.propagationEvaluatorLawsWith`,
`Conformance.codecLaws` and `EncodingProfileVectors.storedCodecLaws` (D170's forwards, "until the next
breaking cut") go on this cut with their roster rows, census cells and guard labels; `propagationPriorLawsAt`,
`codecLawsAt` and `storedCodecLawsAt` are unchanged, and no law or vector byte moved.

*Decided: opt-in is read off the run, not the source (D189.7).* The roster's `Election` is held to what
`certify` and `certifyStream` RUN over the reference witness, read off the families their results carry
(Phase 515's `LawResult.Family`): a base-run family no aggregate ran, or an opt-in family one did, is
named. The check that read `certify`'s source by regex is deleted; the new one is shown red on a planted
mis-election in each direction.

**Rejected.** A `Stream` taken by the capture journals or by `head` (each would demand a witness it never
reads); keeping the facade as a second surface (D141's byte-identity was the migration's guard, and this
cut moves every path anyway); moving the profile into `Fuaran.Core.OpStream` as its own closed type (that
is the twin again); collapsing the DAG's capability twins into the stream.

## 2026-10-20 — D188: a refusal's sentence is a projection of its code, expectation and detail, and hosts certify on code and path; every canonical byte rule is a named `Rendering`, the cross-host form among them, behind one writer, one guard and one canonicity predicate

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 520** (the redesign pass's A §8 slices 5 and 6, §5.3 and §5.4; the operator's 2026-10-17 rulings on D99 and D120). `Fuaran.Core.Wire`: `DecodeError.fs`, `Decoder.fs`, `EncodingProfile.fs`, `Json.fs`, `Canonical.fs` (`Canon.fs` folded in and deleted), `FloatLayout.fs`, `Versioning.fs`, `Codec.fs`; `Fuaran.Core.Idl`: `Decode.fs`, `Declare.fs`, `Artifact.fs`, `Proposal.fs`, `Encode.fs`; `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen` (`FSharpCodec.fs`, `FSharpCollecting.fs`: the generated decode prelude); `Fuaran.Core.Function` / `Fuaran.Core.Query` (the seam codecs' sentences); `Fuaran.Core.Conformance` (`EncodingProfileVectors`, a column per rendering). Amends D99 and D120. Rides the `0.39.0` draft under Breaking.

**Context.** D99 kept "the sentence beside the code" so a codec moved onto the typed layer read the same to every caller. At 0.38.1 that rule was the largest source of accidental code in the wire area: three private adapter layers (`Artifact.fs`, `Proposal.fs`, `Idl/Decode.fs`), `DecodeError.reword`, `Decoder.tagDispatchWith` and `oneOfWith`, and the seam codecs' own `<what><tag>` and "unknown member … in …" spellings all existed to re-spell a typed refusal the way a string form once had, and the generated hosts and the reference host's envelope fixtures were bound to Core's prose (`Versioning.parse`'s "malformed profile" prefix was what a host's fixture matched on). D120 named the profile an escape dialect only: the sorted cross-host form every host hashes (`Canon.render`) had no name, no canonicity predicate, and its own guard chain beside three others.

**Decision.**

1. **The sentence is a projection.** `DecodeError.sentence : DecodeCode -> expected -> detail -> string` writes ONE form per code — `not valid JSON: <detail>`, `missing property: <name>`, `expected <kind>, got <kind>`, `unknown <what>; expected <set>`, and `<class>: <detail>; expected <what>` for the rest — and `DecodeError.make`, `Decoder.fail` and `andThen`'s triple take the DETAIL (what was found), never a sentence. `DecodeError` keeps the shape D99 froze (`Message` stays a field), but nothing re-spells it: `reword`, `tagDispatchWith`, `oneOfWith` and the adapter layers are deleted, and `Idl/Decode`, `Artifact` and `Proposal` read through `Decoder.field` / `list` / `tagDispatch` / `oneOf`. Hosts certify on `Code` and `Path` (which D99's reject family already pinned); a sentence may be reworded between drafts, a code or a path may not. No refusal code or path moved: the reject and refusal corpora are byte-identical, and every sentence-pinning test was re-pinned to code, path and the projected sentence.
2. **A refusal at an owner's path.** `Declare.errors` (and `wireShapeErrors`, `enumWireErrors`, `hostedWireErrors`) answer `VocabularyFault { At; Detail }` — `At` the declaration's position in the vocabulary's lists, which is its `idl.json` path — and `Artifact.ofJsonDetailed` answers a LIST, one `SchemaFault` per fault at its path, where it answered one root refusal whose sentence numbered them. A declared default is checked through the encoder's GUARDED renderer, so a default the encoder refuses to write is refused at its declaration. `Declare.enumAnnotate` and `Proposal.validate` keep their string lists: a lone enum and a proposal document have no vocabulary path to name.
3. **A typed envelope refusal.** `Versioning.parse` / `decode` answer `EnvelopeRefusal`: `Malformed` (the decode refusal, code and path) or `ForeignProfile` at `$.$profile` for a `$profile` that names no capability — WIRE_FORMAT §15.2's one fact, as a value rather than a sentence prefix. `Versioning.Profile` is renamed `Versioning.Capability`, with no alias, so "profile" means a byte rule.
4. **One rendering contract (D120 amended).** `Rendering = { Escape: StringEscape; Order: MemberOrder; Floats: FloatRule }`, each a closed union, and four NAMED values: `V1` and `V2` (the store profiles, `Rendering.ofProfile`), `CrossHost` (`Canon.render`'s bytes) and `Declared` (`Canon.renderOrdered`'s). `Canonical.write` / `tryWrite` / `isCanonical` take a `Rendering`, so the cross-host form now has a canonicity predicate; `Canon` is folded into `Canonical` with no forwards (`Canonical.typed`, `FloatLayout.canonical`). D120's rule stands: the named values are closed and versioned, and a new byte rule is a new NAME. `EncodingProfileVectors` pins a column per rendering, measured from the `0.38.1` binaries before the fold. `EncodingProfile` stays the name a store declares; `OpStream.EncodingProfile` leaves with Phase 516.
5. **One guard.** `Json.firstRenderFault` is the one function over the three classes no canonical rendering survives (a non-finite float, an ill-formed string, a repeated member), in one priority, typed (`RenderFault`), and `Json.tryRender`, `Canonical.tryWrite` and the IDL encoder's `render` refuse through it in one sentence (`RenderFault.describe`), where each carried its own copy of the chain. The encoder alone admits a non-finite float, because its float slots spell one as WIRE_FORMAT §7's quoted token.

**Consequences.** Most refusal sentences change wording (the 0.39.0 notes map every removed and retyped name); `Json.tryRender`'s sentence now names the path. A generated F# host's decode prelude passes the kind found and the interpreter's detail, so its refusals read as the interpreter's; a host that regenerates sees its prelude, the renamed calls and the stamp move. A journal that stored a refusal (`QueryError.UnreadableArgs` carries `DecodeError.toJson`) reads its stored sentence back verbatim, so an append-once journal replays across the change, and a parse refusal journalled today is byte-identical to one journalled at `0.38.1`. The generated TypeScript host's own sentences are B's codegen slices' to project.

## 2026-10-20 — D187: One chain over every record kind (`ChainShape`), one sealed state over an anchor (`Sealed`), one JSONL walk

**Status:** Live

**Context.** Four chained record kinds each carried their own append, walk, rehash and line: the op record (`Chain.fs`), the positional and keyed capture journals (`Capture.fs`), and the sealed snapshot with its compacted and DAG-checkpoint variants (`Snapshot.fs`, `Compacted.fs`, `DagOpStream.fs`, where the checkpoint obtained its seal by asking the snapshot verifier what hash an unsealed snapshot should have carried). The line scanner had a second object reader (`membersOf`) and a third container reader (`stringsField`) beside its structural walk, and the DAG held copies of the linear load's `carry` and `settle` because the linear ones were internal (D83's implicit rule). Redesign pass C (§5.6, §8 slices 6 and 7).

**Decision.**
1. `ChainShape<'R>` (`SeqOf`, `PrevOf`, `HashOf`, `PayloadOf`, `Link`) and `Anchor` (`Seq`, `PrevHash`) are public. `ChainShape.walk` / `tip` / `linkAt` / `append` / `rehash` are written once over a shape at an anchor; the op record (`ChainShape.records cfg encode`), both capture journals and a sealed state are instances. The fifth field, `Link` (the record re-linked), is beyond the pass's four projections: without it neither `append` nor `rehash` can be written over the shape, and `PayloadOf` must not read the link, so re-linking never changes a payload.
2. `Sealed<'State>` (`Anchor`, `State`, `Mode`, `Seal`) is the one sealed state: a `Snapshot` is it at its stream boundary (`Sealed.ofSnapshot` / `toSnapshot`), a compacted stream's snapshot likewise, and a DAG checkpoint is it strict at `{ Seq = 0; PrevHash = node }`. `Sealed.seal` is the one sealing step and `Sealed.firstBreak` the one seal-then-tail verifier (the seal walked as a one-record chain by the one walker). `Snapshot` and `Dag.Checkpoint` keep their records and every verb: the slot is additive, and the record merge is Phase 516's to weigh with the facade.
3. Every chained line is its canonical hash payload with `prevHash` and `hash` spliced in as its last two members, and every chained reader reads `seq`, the kind's own members, then the link. The keyed capture journal gains that JSONL (`KeyedCapture.toJsonl` / `tryToJsonl` / `ofJsonl`, a typed `JsonlFault`).
4. The line scanner has ONE structural walk; its depth-0 frame records its members' (or items') spans, and `membersOf` (the line's own object, `Truncated` at the end of the line within that frame), `stringsField` and `actorField` read those spans. `Capture`'s private `unquote` is `Jsonl.unquote`.
5. `Jsonl.checkedLines`, `Jsonl.carry` and `Jsonl.settle` are public, on a public concern module (`Fuaran.Core.Jsonl`) rather than as facade forwards, since Phase 516 deletes the facade; `settle` is over any read (`decode`, `site`), so the DAG's load is the linear one and its copies are deleted. This answers D83's "the DAG's are its own because the linear ones are internal".
6. No seal, chain hash, line byte or JSONL refusal position moves. One verdict moves, on hand-built data only: a keyed refusal value carrying anything after its JSON string (the private `unquote` wrapped it in an object and read the tail as members) is `Undecodable`.
7. Phases 488 and 491 are rules of this model, not new functions: 488's `firstChainBreakFrom` is `ChainShape.walk` at a segment's `Anchor`, and its `tryRehashMap` is `ChainShape.rehash` with a map; 491's attestation descriptor is a sealed record over an `Anchor`, a head and a party, sealed by the one chain/seal rule.

**Consequences.** `proofs/OpStreamLoad.fst` re-points `members_loop` (obj_members' clauses at depth 0, with `first`) and `strings_field` (an `arr_items`-shaped `items_loop` recording item spans); no theorem statement changes, and `Chain.fst` §7 and `compact_compose` are untouched. Phase 516 folds `ChainShape` / `Sealed` into its one `Stream` value; the facade's two encoding-profile rehash loops and its `walkChain` adapter are left to it.

## 2026-10-20 — D186: the pipeline's dirty set is `Propagation`'s closure instantiated at the pipeline's edges — in the model, which opens `Propagation` instead of restating it, and in the name, `dependencyMap` replacing the `dirtySet` forward; amends D173.2

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 544.** `Fuaran.Core.Function` (`CapabilityPipeline.fs`), `Fuaran.Core.Conformance` (`PipelineSeamLaws.fs`, `Families.fs`), `proofs/Capability.fst`, `proofs/modules.json`, the oracle project and `proofs.json`; rides the `0.39.0` draft (docs/releases/0.39.0.md, Breaking). `api/Fuaran.Core.Function.txt` loses `CapabilityPipeline.dirtySet` and gains `CapabilityPipeline.dependencyMap`; no journalled key, refusal sentence or wire byte moves, and `evalFrom`'s answers are unchanged.

**D186.1 — one model of the closure.** Until this phase `proofs/Capability.fst` carried the propagation closure a second time — the inverted map, the frontier loop, its termination measure and `dirty_closed` — line for line the same as `proofs/Propagation.fst`'s, and held equal to it by nothing but the differential's sampling. The Capability model now `open`s `Propagation` and states the INSTANTIATION instead: `deps_of ns` is the pipeline's dependency map (each node to the ids its `FromNode` edges name), `pipeline_edge_iff` proves its edges are exactly the pipeline's, and `pipeline_dirty_sound` / `pipeline_dirty_least` are `dirty_sound` / `dirty_least` read at the pipeline. `pipeline_evalfrom_agrees` keeps its statement and rests on `Propagation.dirty_closed` over the instance; leastness, which the model's header listed as NOT CLAIMED of the pipeline, is a theorem of it because it is the same loop. The roster and the oracle project check and compile `Propagation` ahead of `Capability`; the set helpers the copy was written for are read from `Propagation` and the module's own section-0 vocabulary (`outcome`, `assoc`, `has_key`, `keys`) stays, because the oracle host names it.

**D186.2 — one name for the closure, and the map it runs over is public.** D173.2 kept `CapabilityPipeline.dirtySet` as a one-line forward because removing it reached surfaces outside Phase 510's region. The forward is removed on the same breaking cut, and what is published instead is the pipeline's map in the shape `Propagation` reads, `CapabilityPipeline.dependencyMap p` (a repeated id to the union of its nodes' edges): the dirty set is `Propagation.dirtyFromChangedIds (dependencyMap p) changed`, written the same way by `evalFrom`, the minimal re-invocation law, the differential and the tests. Four readers needed the edges in that shape, so a public map is the rule-of-three answer rather than three copies of an edge extraction; it is the `Function` -> `Propagation` seam of D173.1 given its name, and it lets the differential compare the instantiation (the two maps' edge relations) before the closure, model against production. The law family `Conformance.capabilityPipelineIncrementalLaws` keeps its id, laws, guard and 600 cases; the downstream law registry sees no change.

**D186.3 — what is not done.** `Propagation.fst` itself is unchanged: the instance reads it and adds nothing to it. The model does not union a repeated id's edges as production does; both name one edge relation, stated in the ladder row's boundary, and `typeCheck` refuses a repeated id before any evaluator consults the map.

## 2026-10-20 — D185: `ObserverState` is opaque, so its order cannot drift from its entries; the defect family that named a drifted state and the checked walk that refused one are removed; applies D117.3

**Status:** Live

**Context.** D117.3 made the function registry opaque because a public record lets `{ r with … }` bypass every verb that keeps a derived index honest, and left three registry records public because they carry no derived index. `ObserverState` was the case the rule names and the record did not follow: its `Order` is a derived index of `Entries` (exactly the keys, each once, oldest registration first), both fields were public, and Phase 383 paid for that with `ObserverDefect` (`UnregisteredInOrder`, `RepeatedInOrder`, `UnorderedEntry`) and `ObserverWitness.tryObserveTree`, a walk that checked a hand-built state first. Read at the base tree, every one of the three cases was a state no verb produces: `register` appends an id only when it is absent, `update` never touches the order, and `unregister` removes the entry and the id together. The family existed to describe states only the record's publicity made constructible.

**D185.1 — the representation is private (applies D117.3).** `ObserverState`'s record is `private`; `ObserverWitness.empty`, `register`, `update` and `unregister` are its only constructors, and two readers are added: `isRegistered st nodeId` (what `snapshot` answers `Some` for) and `registered st` (the ids in registration order, the order `observeTree` walks each level in). The order is kept by the verbs as before, not recomputed: a registration sequence number would make it derivable from the entries alone, but it would also make two states holding the same registrations unequal by a counter (`register a` then `unregister a` would no longer equal `empty`), and the only writers already keep the list exact.

**D185.2 — the drift family is removed, not kept as a guard.** `ObserverDefect` had no case that is not drift, so the union is removed whole, with `tryObserveTree`; `observeTree` is unchanged and needs no totality clause over a state it cannot be handed. `ObserverEntry` becomes internal: it was the element type of the public map and nothing else builds or reads one. A host that read `state.Entries` to test membership calls `isRegistered`; a declared parent is not exposed — the host declared it, no consumer reads it back, and a reader can be added additively when one does.

**D185.3 — the observer law reads the readers.** `Conformance.observerLawsAt` keeps its two cells; its first cell also holds `isRegistered` to `snapshot` and `registered` to the script's surviving registrations, oldest first. The family's id, cell count and export are unchanged.

## 2026-10-20 — D184: one rule registry, `Validator.Rules<'Subject,'Id>`, over the registration-ordered lattice; the column validator's registry is its instance at a table, the fifth registry; one walker; amends D117

**Status:** Live

**Context.** D117 made a registry a lattice and counted four (`CapabilityRegistry`, `FunctionRegistry`, `QueryRegistry`, `Validator.RuleRegistry`). A fifth, `ColumnValidator.Registry`, had `empty` / `enumerate` / `tryFind` / `register` / `ofRules` and none of the lifecycle, and the validator package walked rules three ways (`runAllTagged`, `runPack`, `ColumnValidator.validateTagged`), each with its own loop over the `RULE-FAULT` guard. `ColumnRule` and `PackCheck` were one shape under two field names. The operator ruled (3A) on 2026-10-17: the column registry comes onto the lattice and D117 counts five.

**Decision.**
1. **`Validator.Rules<'Subject,'Id>` is the one rule registry**: registration-ordered, of `PackCheck`s over any subject, with a private representation so one rule per id holds by construction, and the verbs `empty` / `enumerate` / `tryFind` / `register` / `unregister` / `replace` / `restrict` / `union` / `ofChecks` refusing in `RegistrationError`, plus `run`, the walk.
2. **The lifecycle over a list is written once** (`Validator.Ordered`, internal) and carries both list-ordered registries, `RuleRegistry` and `Rules`. It is `KeyedRegistry`'s twin, not a use of it: a validator registry's order is its run order (D117.2), and the validator package does not reference `Fuaran.Core.Function`. So the five registries stand on one lattice in two orders and no verb is hand-written.
3. **One walker** (`Validator.walk`, internal): `runAllTagged`, `runPack` and `Rules.run` (and so `ColumnValidator.validateTagged`) are it — stamp, guard, order.
4. **`ColumnRule` is `PackCheck<Table, string>` and `ColumnValidator.Registry` is `Rules<Table, string>`** (removal-class on the 0.39.0 draft; no consumer outside the repository used either record). The column module keeps its verb names as the column vocabulary over `Rules`, as the seams' registries keep theirs over `Seam` (D172), and gains `unregister` / `replace` / `restrict` / `union`.
5. **`RuleFamily` and `RuleRegistry` are NOT retyped.** `RuleFamily.Run` takes the witness at run time, so it cannot be an alias of `PackCheck` without retyping it and `perNode`, and consumers build it by record literal; it enters the framework through `Validator.asCheck w family`. Its retype waits for the 1.0 cut.
6. **Every stock defect code is a `[<Literal>]`** (`ColumnValidator.NoColumnCode`, `NotNullCode`, `OfTypeCode`, `InRangeCode`, `UniqueCode` join the existing nine); no code is spelled inline. The spellings are unchanged.
7. **`inRange` and `unique` read the typed storage, not through `TypeOps`.** `inRange` is an element loop, and D145.5 / D178 keep element loops on monomorphic typed arms and the row to scalar functions; `unique` reads each key cell with `Column.cell`. Neither needs the internal row, so `TypeOps` stays internal to `Fuaran.Core.Column`: no `InternalsVisibleTo`, no published row.
8. **fuaran-core#489's recovery fields ride a sidecar on the walk's result** — `Finding<'Id> = { Defect; Guidance: RejectionGuidance option }`, as `PackFinding` wraps a defect and as `PolicyDenial` carries guidance beside a refusal — never a field on `Defect`.

**Consequences.** Every defect code, finding and order is unchanged and no conformance vector moves. `RegistryLifecycleTests` names each lifecycle case on five registries. `Conformance.registryLaws` samples all five (five cells of its own for the column registry, so the export's `cases` for that family moves 2200 -> 3200). A rule over any subject now has the gate the others pass through, and a defect's recovery fields attach in one place.

**Amends:** D117 (the count is five; the fifth stands on the registration-ordered twin of the lattice).

## 2026-10-20 — D183: One read surface — `ReadOptions` and four readers; the string-error twin deleted

**Status:** Live

Wire read text through eleven parse entry points over one scanner, a `Json.ReadError` beside `DecodeError`, and the string-error `Decode` module kept "for one draft" at Phase 310 (redesign pass A section 5.2, section 8 slices 3 and 4). Ruled (Phase 519): one read surface. `ReadOptions = { Null: NullPolicy; Limits: JsonLimits }`, with `ReadOptions.strict` (`RejectNull`, `JsonLimits.depthOnly 512`) and `ReadOptions.tolerantOfNull` named; four readers: `Json.read : ReadOptions -> string -> Result<JVal, JsonRefusal>` (the parser's native answer and the only parser-side union), `Json.parse : string -> Result<JVal, string>` (strict, the one string form), `Reader.read : ReadOptions -> (Reader -> 'a) -> string -> Result<'a, DecodeError>` and `Decoder.parse : ReadOptions -> string -> Result<JVal, DecodeError>`. `Json.ReadError` is deleted: a shape mismatch is `WrongKind` at the path of the value, read off the scanner's frames, and the rule "a refusal anywhere in the document outranks a mismatch" (D121) stands. `DecodeError.ofJsonError` folds into the one `DecodeError.ofJsonRefusal`, which places every breach at its path; the depth cap is therefore a `Depth` breach at the container opened past it on every reader, where the strict readers reported it at the root — the one behavioural move, classed breaking, consistent with WIRE_FORMAT section 21.2 rule 2. `Decode.fs` is deleted with no forwards (the open 0.39.0 slot is the one breaking cut, so "forwards for one draft" collapses into this phase); `ColumnCodec` and `SchemaDeltaCodec` read through `Decoder` with a `DecodeError -> ColumnError` projection of their own, every spelling unchanged, and keep the cap as `NotJson`/`MaxDepthExceeded`. Rejected: a strict `Decoder.parse : string -> …` beside an options form (two readers for one refusal type); `[<Obsolete>]` forwards (a removal the release notes map is cheaper for consumers who raise once); a `ColumnError` limit case (a union-widening that moves the column model's bridge for no refusal a strict read can meet beyond the cap). `JsonErrorKind.MaxDepthExceeded` stays as the scanner's signal and the parser model's case. The generated decoders follow: the F# codec passes `ReadOptions.strict`; the TypeScript reader keeps a path stack and throws the breach at it.

## 2026-10-20 — D182: the diff is one run of the emitter's passes and refuses through `Rejection`; under a keyed scope a holder's keyed subtrees are its content; a tree carrying an id twice has no index

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 518** (the redesign pass's C §8 slices 4 and 5, with the keyed diff carried from
fuaran-core#496.t6). `Fuaran.Core.Ops`: `Diff.fs`, `Rejection.fs`, `Ops.fs` (`Index.afterOp`, `firstUncontained`);
`Fuaran.Core.Tree`: `Tree.fs` (`Index`, `Digests`, the rebuild engine); `Fuaran.Core.Projection`;
`Fuaran.Core.AiSurface` (`RejectionCodec`); `Fuaran.Core.Conformance` (`changeLaws` removed, `keyedDiffLawsAt`
added). Extends D112 (a classification is a projection of the diff) and D181 (the keyed `Diff` it named). Rides
the `0.39.0` draft under Breaking.

**Context.** `Diff.changes` walked both trees a second time and `Conformance.changeLaws` held it equal to the
script, a second implementation kept equal by a law. `DiffError`'s cases mirrored three of `Rejection`'s
(`DuplicateIdInTree`, `TargetNotAContainer`, `IllegalChildInTree`) under other names, so a host that forwarded a
refusal wrote two vocabularies for one fact. The diff had no keyed form: over the structural witness a change below a
keyed position was invisible to an own-content encoder, and over `Tree.traversal` its shells under-filled the keyed
arity (`KeyedGateDiffTests` (b), (c)). And `Tree.Index` answered one malformed tree three ways: `build` kept the
last occurrence of a repeated id, `tryBuild` refused it, `isFreshFor` certified nothing.

**Decision.**

1. **One run, two readings.** The emitter's passes record, at the site each pass decides a fact, the `Change` that
   fact is; `toOps` / `toOpsWith` read the script and `changes` the classification off the same run. `changes`
   takes `encode policy scope`, as `toOpsWith` does, so it refuses exactly where the script does. `changeLaws` has
   nothing left to hold equal: it leaves the kit and its checks are a unit test (`ContentDiffTests`).
2. **`DiffError` folds into `Rejection`.** The three mirror cases are `DuplicateId`, `NotAContainer` and
   `IllegalChild` (same payloads); `RootIdMismatch of before * after` is a new case declared last, raised by `Diff`
   alone. The refusal order is unchanged. `RejectionCodec` writes it as `rootIdMismatch`. A new case rather than a
   `Rejected` code because it is a skeleton fact every host can name, and `Rejected` is the domain's extension point.
3. **The keyed diff locates through the keyed walk and edits through the structural witness**, as the engine does
   (D81, D181). Its repeated-id and containment checks read `Tree.traversal`; its shells empty structural children
   only, so no keyed position is vacated. A holder's keyed subtrees are its CONTENT, which is what an `UpdateNode`
   payload is under the keyed engine: a change anywhere below a keyed position is the holder's `UpdateNode`
   (`changes`: the holder `Changed`), whatever the caller's encoder reads, because the diff compares the keyed
   subtrees node by node. Finer granularity (an `UpdateNode` of the node inside the keyed subtree, structural ops
   inside it) was considered and not taken: it needs an ordering between keyed-content updates and structural ops
   that the canHold placement rule (D103) can contradict, for no answer a consumer has asked for.
4. **A relocation across a keyed boundary is refused, as `KeyedPosition`.** A node the two trees carry on different
   sides of a keyed boundary (in or below a holder's keyed positions in one, elsewhere in the other) needs the
   holder's update ordered against the structural ops on both sides of it, and a swap between two holders has no
   order at all. It is the same domain edit `KeyedPosition` already names on the apply path, so the diff reuses the
   case (the first such node in `before`'s keyed preorder, the holder that carries it, the slot) rather than mint a
   second spelling of one fact.
5. **`Tree.Index.build` refuses a repeated id** (`Result<NodeIndex, 'Id>`) and `tryBuild` is removed: one answer at
   every entry point that makes an index. `Ops.Index.afterOp` returns its fallback's `Result`. `isFreshFor` reads
   uniqueness through the one scan (`firstRepeat`). `Index.path` KEEPS its cycle guard: `NodeIndex` is a public
   record a caller can build by hand and `rebind` outside its contract can link a node under its own descendant, so
   the guard still stands for totality although `build` no longer makes the cycle.
6. **`Tree.Digests` maps hold `Digest`** (and `ownDigest` / `frameDigest` return one), each `Hex` byte-identical to
   the string the maps held. `Tree.digests` stays total over a malformed tree, because `Projection` renders one by
   design; `ProjectionSnapshot` keeps its hex maps (a consumer-persisted baseline with no defect behind a retype).
7. **One rebuild engine.** `Tree.map` and `FreshIds.repairDuplicates` share one postorder engine that hands each
   node its preorder position and does not rebuild a leaf (a conformant witness answers `ReplaceChildren n []`
   with `n`; one partial on leaves cannot answer it at all).

**Consequences.** Breaking on the draft: `DiffError` removed, `Diff.changes` retyped, `Rejection` widened,
`Tree.Index.build` and `Ops.Index.afterOp` retyped, `Tree.Index.tryBuild` removed, the digest maps retyped,
`Conformance.changeLaws` removed (its row leaves `docs/conformance-families.json`, which a downstream registry and
the consumers' censuses read) and `Conformance.keyedDiffLawsAt` added. No `conformance/` vector moves; the proof
models are unchanged (the diff bridge renders the moved cases under the model's names).

## 2026-10-20 — D181: the engine is four verbs over two records — `Policy` (grammar, references) and `OpScope` (structural witness, ids, `CanHold`, keyed positions); every combination exists by construction, the old per-combination names are removed, `CanHold` is asked of every parent an op writes, and a keyed-position refusal names its slot by index

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 517** (the redesign pass's C §8 slice 3, both halves; absorbs fuaran-core#492's two rules on
the operator's ruling of 2026-10-20). `Fuaran.Core.Ops`: `Ops.fs` (`OpScope`, `Policy`, the internal `Walks`,
`apply` / `canApply` / `applyAll` / `canApplyAll`, `footprint` / `footprintIn`), `Diff.fs`, `TreePlacement.fs`,
`Arbitration.fs`, `WriteGate.fs`, `Rejection.fs`; `Fuaran.Core.AiSurface` (`RejectionCodec`);
`Fuaran.Core.Conformance` (`KeyedApplyLaws.fs`, the keyed-lock law); `proofs/Preservation.fst` (the contained
engine's reorder arm, tracking production). Amends D177; extends D38's ordering to the reorder clause. Rides the
`0.39.0` draft under Breaking.

**Context.** The op engine was a matrix: plain, contained and keyed scopes; grammar and reference policies; single
and script; do and dry run. It was spelled as 39 named entries across `Ops`, `Diff`, `TreePlacement`,
`Arbitration` and `WriteGate`, and eight cells had no entry at all (keyed scripts, keyed grammar, keyed references,
keyed `Diff`, keyed placement, keyed gate, keyed arbitration composed by hand). A keyed write could therefore
bypass a check the plain path made by choosing which spelling to call. The write gate walked the structural witness
only, so a lock on a node that holds keyed positions did not reach the nodes held in them (the redesign pass's 7.2,
pinned as a limit by Phase 496). The reorder clause never asked `canHold` (7.7), so a domain kept a childless-reorder
pre-check beside the engine. And `KeyedPosition` named the holder but not which position, so a domain kept its own
"that slot is not structural" refusal.

**Decision.**

1. **Two records.** `OpScope` is how the engine sees a domain's tree: the structural witness (`Nodes`), the id
   witness (`Ids`), which nodes can hold children (`CanHold`, `None` = every node), and the keyed positions
   (`Keyed`, a `KeyedWitness`). `Policy` is which checks run beyond the engine's own: the containment grammar
   (`Grammar`) and the references (`Refs`). The split follows the shard: a scope is a fact about the domain's
   tree, which every reader of it (the engine, the footprint, the gate, placement, arbitration, the diff) must
   share; a policy is a set of refusals a caller opts into. Builders: `OpScope.plain` / `contained` / `keyed`,
   `Policy.none` / `grammar` / `referenced`; a caller combines a grammar with references as
   `{ Policy.grammar g with Refs = Some r }`.
2. **Named `OpScope`, not `Scope`.** `Fuaran.Core.Scope<'Id>` (a projection's scope, `Fuaran.Core.Projection`)
   already shares the namespace, and a caller opening both packages would meet FS1124 ("multiple types exist
   called 'Scope'") on every `Scope.Whole` it already writes — measured on a two-type fixture before the name was
   chosen. `TreePlacement` was named against `Placement` for the same reason (Phase 312). `Policy` clashes with
   nothing in the namespace and keeps the shard's name.
3. **The public `OpScope` is the declaration; the walks are derived.** D177's internal `OpScope` (edit witness,
   locate witness, keyed function, id witness) is now the internal `Walks`, which the engine derives from the
   public record once per entry (`Tree.traversal` when keyed positions are declared). The public record carries
   the `KeyedWitness` rather than a locate witness so a caller cannot hand the engine a locate walk that disagrees
   with its keyed positions, and so the keyed `Diff` (fuaran-core#518) has `ReplaceKeyedChildren` to rebuild
   through. `OpView` and the runner stay internal (D177's reason stands: no reader outside the package).
4. **Four verbs, the old names removed in the same cut.** `Ops.apply` / `canApply` / `applyAll` / `canApplyAll`
   take `policy scope` first; so do `Ops.footprint` / `footprintIn`, `Diff.toOps` / `toOpsWith` (the encoder
   first, as before), `TreePlacement.place` / `move` / `clone`, `Arbitration.arbitrate` / `arbitrateIn` /
   `interference`, and `WriteGate.applyGated` (after the gate); `WriteGate.targetsOf` / `decide` take the scope.
   Every `…Contained`, `…Keyed`, `…Grammar`, `…Referenced`, `applyAllWith` and `canApplyAllWith` name is removed
   rather than kept as a forward: the `0.39.0` draft is the breaking cut the slice's second step waited for, and
   two spellings of one entry were the defect. The refusal order inside one step is the engine's whichever
   fields are set: the engine's checks (D38), then the grammar, then the references. The verdict of every
   existing combination is unchanged (the apply corpus, `KeyedApplyLaws`' identity law and every family hold old
   ≡ new); the new combinations (keyed with a grammar or references, keyed placement, keyed arbitration over a
   keyed well-formed base, a gate under any scope) are what the records give by construction.
5. **`CanHold` is asked of every parent the view says an op writes, reorder included.** A reorder's parent is
   checked LAST, after the permutation check, so no refused reorder changes class (D38's ordering); the one
   verdict that moves is an ACCEPTED reorder of a node `canHold` refuses (the empty reorder of a leaf, and a
   permutation under a node already in violation), now `NotAContainer(parent, kind)`. A remove's source parent is
   not asked: removing a child cannot break the invariant, and refusing there would be an invariant-repair gate
   (D38's reasoning for not walking a moved subtree). `proofs/Preservation.fst`'s contained engine gains the same
   clause (a model tracking production; no theorem statement moves).
6. **The write gate reads ancestors along the scope's walk.** Under a keyed scope a target's chain runs through
   its holder, so a lock on a holder covers its keyed subtree, and the gate steps the scope's own engine. The
   keyed-lock law is in `Conformance.keyedApplyLawsAt`, the keyed family, because `writeGateLaws` takes no keyed
   witness and widening its witness list would move its declared signature in the roster export.
7. **`KeyedPosition` carries its slot: `target * holder * slot: int`** (the widening, not a new case — a closed
   union gaining a case breaks every exhaustive match too, and would leave `KeyedPosition` never raised). The slot
   is the position's 0-based index in the holder's `KeyedChildren` list. An index rather than a label because the
   `KeyedWitness` declares an ordered list and carries no labels; were labels ever declared, the index would still
   be what locates the position, so a label would be an addition beside it, never a replacement.
   `RejectionCodec` writes it as `slot`; no conformance vector carries the case, so no corpus byte moves.

**Consequences.** Breaking for every caller of an engine entry (the Migration line in `docs/releases/0.39.0.md`
maps each old name), for a positional `KeyedPosition` pattern or construction, and for a caller that relied on an
accepted reorder under a node `canHold` refuses. The keyed `Diff` remains a stated limit: the diff walks a scope's
structural witness whatever its keyed positions (`KeyedGateDiffTests` (b) and (c)); fuaran-core#518 carries it.
`Ops.invert` / `invertAll` / `normalize` / `lower` keep their witness parameters: they are not engine entries of
the matrix and are plain-scope by contract.

## 2026-10-20 — D180: a law result carries its kind, its family, its evidence and its reach; nothing reads its prose to learn them, and a consumer builds one with a constructor

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 515** (the redesign pass's E §8 slice 1; the operator's ruling A on the `LawResult`
open decision, 2026-10-17). `Fuaran.Core.Conformance`: `LawResult.fs` (`LawKind`, `LawResult`, the
`LawResult` module), `SampleAdequacy.fs`, `LawKit.fs`, `Conformance.fs`, the vector modules. Amends D78,
which declined the widening on the `0.33.0` draft; rides the `0.39.0` draft under Breaking.

**Context.** `LawResult` was `{ Law; Passed; Counterexample }`, so everything the kit needed to know about a
result beyond pass or fail was spelled into the two strings and parsed back: a guard by its law opening
`sample adequacy (`, the family that emitted it by the text up to `): `, the dimension it guarded by the
sentence after, a never-reached law by its counterexample opening `never reached`, a declared vacuity by
prose appended to a guard's dimension, a corpus law by a fragment of its name, and a covered cell's guard
by a regex over the kit's sources. Measured at the phase's head: 50 prose recognisers across `src` and
`tests` (the pass counted 43 by a narrower method; both lists are in the phase record), and the hand lists
that grew beside them — `drawnRefusalSix`'s restated dimensions, `zeroVectorRuns`' name fragments and the
`coveredDimensions` source scan. A green guard said nothing about how often it was reached, because the
record had nowhere to put the counts.

**Decision.**

1. **The record gains four fields, after the three it had** (so the change is a record widening and moves
   no field's position): `Family` (the roster key of the family whose run produced it), `Kind`, `Evidence`
   (the assertions the verdict stands on) and `Reached` (a guard's counts, demanded then beside, on the
   green path as on the red). `Kind` is a closed union, `LawKind`: `Subject of coveredBy: string option`
   (a law about the witness; `Some` names the guard dimension that reports its zero), `Guard of dimension`,
   `Corpus of what` (a fixed corpus's or a store's non-emptiness law) and `Declared of what` (a side vacuous
   BY DECLARATION).
2. **The runner fills the four; nothing parses `Law`.** `LawCell.Result` sets the kind and the evidence (a
   recorded counterexample counts as an assertion, so a red law at zero evidence is exactly the
   never-reached verdict); the guard constructors (`SampleAdequacy.reached`, `reachedBeside`,
   `reachedFraction`, `spanned`) set the guard's dimension, counts and family; every public entry point
   labels the subject laws it ran with its runner's id (`Conformance`'s forwards through one `within`, the
   fixed-corpus modules at their entry points), and a delegate's guard keeps the delegate's id. `cases`,
   `certify`, `certifyStream`, `QuerySeamLaws` and the vacuity suite read the fields.
3. **A declared vacuity is a `Declared` result, not a dimension suffix.** D100's recorded waiver in
   `keyedArbitrationLawsWith` is two results, `Declared "container capability"` and `Declared "keyed
   position"`, beside a guard whose dimension no longer carries prose; `keyedApplyLawsAt` (`keyed
   position`) and `footprintLawsAt` (`slot access`) say theirs the same way, and `LawKit.declared` takes
   the `what`. The law text of each declared line is the sentence the suffix used to carry, so a reader
   who matched the words still finds them.
4. **The constructors are the stable surface.** `LawResult.subject family law evidence counterexample` (the
   general one), `pass`, `fail`, `guard` and `declared`, with `isAdequacy`, `isNeverReached` and
   `withFamily` as the readers. A consumer's literal `{ Law = l; Passed = cx.IsNone; Counterexample = cx }`
   is `LawResult.subject "<Module>.<entry>" l n cx`, where `n` is the number of times the law was asserted
   (at least one for a law that was checked: a red law with zero evidence reads as never reached).
5. **`SampleAdequacy.guardOpening` leaves the public surface** (it was the recogniser's key; the prefix is
   still how a guard's statement opens, through `lawPrefix`). The remedy sentence is spelled once
   (`SampleAdequacy.widenTheGenerator`), so the never-reached remedy and the guard's remedy end in the same
   words.
6. **The census cell does not move.** `cases` still counts the subject and corpus laws a run reported times
   its iterations, so `docs/conformance-families.{md,json}` re-emit byte-identical and the downstream
   registry's `(id, cases)` reading is unchanged. `CaseCount.Starved` names a starved guard by its
   dimension, as its documentation always said, where it used to carry the guard's sentence.

**Considered and not taken.** *Counting `Evidence` into `Cases`* (the pass's D-8, which would make a
budget-shaped family's cell exact): it changes the number the downstream registry reads for every family,
which is a contract move on that cell rather than a consequence of the widening, and a consumer's hand-built
law reports whatever evidence it is given; `Evidence` is carried so that move is a separate, deliberate
change. *A `FamilyId` type on the record*: the guard constructors are public and take a string, and
`CaseCount.Family` is a string; one spelling of the id across the record and its census is worth more than
the type. *A runtime refusal of an orphaned covered cell*: the suite checks it per reference run off
`Subject (Some d)` against the run's own guards and corpus laws, which is the same fact without a runner
that owns every cell.

**Why the shape should hold to 1.0.** The record now carries every fact the kit's readers ask of it, each
as data; the constructors absorb a future field, so a field added later moves no consumer that used them.
What would reopen it: a reader that needs to tell a guard's demanded counts from those counted beside them
(today one list, demanded first), or a result that belongs to more than one family.

**Consumers raised in the cohort sweep after the release.** The compute repository builds 49 results by
literal (`DataFrameConformance.fs` 39, `IncrementalDelta.fs` 8, `DeriveTypingLaws.fs` 1,
`PipelineQueryLaws.fs` 1) and the UI tier's .NET host 1 (`CoreIncrementalLawsTests.fs`); each becomes one
`LawResult.subject` call. Neither reads `guardOpening`; the UI tier's census copies the guard opening as its
own literal, which still matches the unchanged law text.

## 2026-10-20 — D179: a declared IDL type is lowered once, to an internal `WireForm` that the encoder, the decoder, the sampler and the validator switch on; the lowering is one level deep, the artifact keeps spelling the declared type, and presence stays `Optionality`

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 513** (the redesign pass's A §5.5 and §8 slice 7). `src/Fuaran.Core.Idl/WireForm.fs`
(`WireForm`, `UnionForm`, `Undeclared`, `WireForm.ofType`, `caseFields`, `jsonKind`, `objectCapable`,
`reachesNodeAtFloor`, `requiredReachesNode`), `Encode.fs` (`encodeValue`), `Decode.fs` (`decodeValue`,
`arity`), `Sample.fs` (`sampleType`, `atFloor`), `Declare.fs` (`hostedWireErrors`, `errors`' type checks)
and `Artifact.fs` (`typeJson`'s sentinels).

**Context.** The encoder, the decoder and the sampler each matched on all eighteen `IdlType` cases (20, 40
and 27 arms), and each resolved what the slot means on the wire for itself: the enum, union or record a
name declares, a union's arguments bound to its parameters and its case's fields substituted (four
copies), which case the harden policy makes transparent, that `TClosure` and `TFn` are one sentinel, and
whether a hosted slot is its declared wire form or verbatim JSON. The validator re-derived the last two
again (`objectCapable`, `hostedWireErrors`' readable forms), and the sampler's depth-floor predicate
mirrored the draw's arms clause for clause by hand. The redesign pass counted "sixty to a hundred"
optionality match sites across the IDL; measured at the parent of this change, that figure is the code
generator's (152 lines naming an `Optionality` case, 65 reads of a field's `Opt`), while this package
holds 38 and 10, most of them the model's own definitions, the artifact's spelling of a field's presence
and the proposal reader.

**Decision.**

1. **One lowering, internal.** `WireForm.ofType idl t` answers what `t` is on the wire: a scalar, a
   resolved enum, a sentinel (the string and the one value it stands for), verbatim JSON, a hosted slot's
   declared wire and format, a resolved union (`UnionForm`: the declaration, the binding or the arity
   fault, the transparent case), a resolved record, a list, a map, a node, a bare kind, an op, an unbound
   variable, or a reference the vocabulary does not declare. `Encode`, `Decode` and `Sample` match on it
   and on no declared case; `Declare`'s reference, arity, transparent-instantiation and hosted-readable
   checks read it; a case's substituted fields are `caseFields`; the decoder's expected JSON kind is
   `jsonKind`. A sweep in `IdlThreeHostTests` holds the three readers off the declared cases and the
   sentinel spellings in `WireForm.fs`, with a control over the lowering itself.
2. **One level deep.** A list's item, a map's value, a hosted slot's wire type and every field type stay
   declared `IdlType`s and are lowered when a reader reaches them. A vocabulary is recursive, so a lowered
   tree would not be finite; and lowering on reach keeps every reader's refusal ORDER, which differs by
   design (the bare-value decoder asks for a transparent case before it reports an arity fault, the
   encoder reports the arity first). The lowering states each fault; the reader orders them. That is why
   an arity fault is data on `UnionForm` rather than a form of its own, and why an undeclared reference
   keeps its kind and a union's arguments.
3. **The depth floor is a fold over the lowering**, `reachesNodeAtFloor`, with the same arms as the draw
   it predicts, and `requiredReachesNode` is the leaf test the kind and op floors share (`atFloor`, one
   filter where there were two). It keeps one over-approximation it inherited: a union reaches when an
   ARGUMENT reaches, whether or not a case the floor draws holds it. Narrowing it moves which draws the
   sampler takes on a vocabulary with that shape, which is a seeded-stream change for a later phase to
   make deliberately, not a by-product of this one.
4. **The artifact spells the declared type.** `idl.json`'s type objects are read back into the
   declaration, so they keep what the wire erases: `closure` and `fn` stay two cases, a union stays
   named and applied, a variable stays a variable. `typeJson` reads only the sentinel spellings from the
   lowering. The redesign pass's "`Artifact.typeJson` switches on `WireForm`" holds for those and is
   false for the rest.
5. **Presence stays `Optionality`** (A §5.5: "`Presence` stays `Optionality`"). A lowered field would be
   the same four cases under another name; the readers keep their one presence match each, and the
   floor's two required-field reads became one.
6. **Internal, with the code generator as the next reader.** No reader outside this package needs it now,
   and publishing it ahead of one would freeze an unused contract (D51; D171, D174, D177 and D178 are the
   precedents). The generator already holds this package's `InternalsVisibleTo`; when its emitters adopt
   the lowering they read it from `NoInlining` functions (D129), and the adopting phase decides whether a
   public type would serve a third-party emitter better. The four decode policies the after-0.34.0 review
   names (strict members, item bounds, an integer range, admission) would attach here as data — on the
   `Record` and `Union` forms, on `List` and `Map`, on `Int`, and on `UnionForm` respectively — rather than
   as `IdlType` cases; none is added.

**Consequences.** No byte moves. A probe of 7,920 sampled nodes and their encode, decode and re-encode over
the suite's eleven vocabularies and the UI tier's committed `idl.json`, every declared field type's encode
and decode against fourteen wrong values and eleven wrong JSON values (with undeclared, unbound,
mis-applied and hosted types added), every refusal sentence and path, every `Declare.errors` finding, every
`Artifact.render` and the whole `ParityVectors` table (the `sample/*` rows among it) was byte-identical
before and after, and differed in 6,344 lines when one `jsonKind` spelling was perturbed. Lines of code
that match a declared `IdlType` case: `Encode` 20 → 0, `Decode` 40 → 0, `Sample` 27 → 0, `Declare` 34 → 8
(the walks that find where a hosted codec or a type variable is declared, and the rule that a host-only
field is a `TFn` — questions about the declaration, not the wire). Optionality sites in this package: 38 →
35 lines naming a case, 10 → 7 reads of a field's `Opt`.

**Rejected.**
- A fully lowered tree (A §5.5's `Record of (IdlField * WireForm) list`). Not finite over a recursive
  vocabulary, and eager: it would report a fault in a slot no value reaches.
- Substitution inside `ofType` (A §5.5's `Map<string, IdlType>` parameter). The binding belongs to the
  union reference, and a case's fields are substituted when that case is reached, as each reader did.
- A presence type beside the lowering. See 5.

## 2026-10-20 — D178: the scalar set is one internal table of rows that every per-column walk reads, and one value outside a table is read and written by `ColumnCodec.readCell` / `writeCell`; the table lives in `Column.fs` and stays internal

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 514** (the redesign pass's D §8 S3 and S5, with S10's `ordinal` item).
`src/Fuaran.Core.Column/Column.fs` (`TypeOps<'T>`, `TypeOpsUser`, `ColumnDataUser`, `TypeOps.ofType`,
`TypeOps.ofData`, `TypeOps.fill`), `ColumnCodec.fs` (`columnJson`, `decodeColumn`, `readCell`,
`writeCell`), `Table.fs` (`firstUncarriableCell`), `ColumnType.fs` (`widens`), `Query.fs`
(`QueryShape.literalJson` / `literalOf`) and `QueryCodec.fs` (`argCell`, `columnRefused`).

**Context.** What one column type does with one value was spelled as a seven-arm match wherever it was
needed: `Column.ofCells` and the codec's decode each filled the typed storage with a walk of their own and a
match beside it, the encoder had a match for the value and another for the absent slot, `Table.validate` a
match for the uncarriable value, and `ColumnType` spelled its order twice (`all`, and a private `ordinal`
for `widens`). A value outside a table — a predicate's literal, a model's argument to a query — was read
and written by building a one-row table document and running the whole codec over it, three times in
`Query` and once in `QueryCodec`, and a refusal the codec named for a query's `source` or a result's `rows`
was dropped.

**Decision.**

1. **One row per scalar type, internal.** `TypeOps<'T>` holds what a type does with one element: the
   storage it allocates, a cell as an element and back, one JSON value read and written, the absent slot,
   the test and the refusal for an element the codec cannot carry, and the storage built over a filled
   array. Two dispatches hand a row to a computation generic over the element type (F# has no
   existential type): `ofType` from a `ColumnType`, `ofData` from a column's storage with the element at
   each row. `fill` is the one walk `ofCells` and decode share; the encoder, `Table.validate`'s scan and
   the one-cell reader and writer read the same rows. A new scalar type is one row and one arm in each
   dispatch. `Column.cell`, the typed builders and readers, `ColumnData`'s members and the aggregate loops
   keep their typed arms: they are the per-row reads and the loops D145.5 measured, not walks a row is
   handed to.
2. **The row holds scalar functions, never an element loop (D145.5).** A timestamp row's element is the
   struct pair its two vectors hold at one row; its `Build` and its view in `ofData` write and read the
   second vector, which is the one place the row is not a single vector. `fill` is `inline`, so each of
   its two callers expands its own loop with the row's reader called directly; measured on .NET at
   100,000 rows, `ofCells` and decode are at or below their old times for every type. `Table.validate`'s
   scan of a float, date or timestamp column costs one more call per present row than its typed arm did
   (1.3 to 1.6 ms became 2.1 to 3.1 ms per 100,000 rows); validation is not on the compute layer's tick
   path, and the scan of an int, bool or string column still reads nothing.
3. **The table lives in `Column.fs`, not `ColumnType.fs`.** A row names `Cell`, `Vector`, `ColumnData`
   and `ColumnError`, all compiled after `ColumnType.fs`, so it cannot live there without moving files
   in the project. The JSON readers moved with it from `ColumnCodec.fs`. `Cell.typeOf`, `compare` and
   `token` keep their matches: they are compiled before the table, they are matches over `Cell`'s eight
   cases rather than over `ColumnType`, and `compare` is a cross-family order (int, float and decimal),
   not a per-type function. `ColumnType.ordinal` is gone: `widens` compares tags, so the scalar set has
   one order, `all`.
4. **`TypeOps` stays internal.** No reader outside `Fuaran.Core.Column` needs it, and publishing it ahead
   of one would freeze an unused contract (D51; D171, D174 and D177 are the precedents). The validator's
   rules (Phase 521) are in `Fuaran.Core.Validator`, which cannot see an internal of this package without
   a friend grant and the `NoInlining` forwarders D129 asks for; that phase decides between the grant and
   a published row when it is the adopter.
5. **One value outside a table is `ColumnCodec.readCell` / `writeCell` (public, additive).** `writeCell
   column ty cell` is the slot the codec writes for the cell in a `ty` column (widened as `ofCells`
   widens it, the absent slot for `Null`), or `ofCells`'s refusal. `readCell column ty value` is the cell
   decode answers for the value at a present row, with the refusal decode names, including the
   non-finite float `Table.validate` ends decode with. A predicate's literal and a query argument are
   read and written through them; every literal byte is unchanged. `columnRefused` carries the
   `ColumnError`'s sentence after the member's.

**Consequences.** Every column wire byte, refusal and corpus file is unchanged; a 4,046-line probe of
encode, decode, validate, `ofCells`, `ofTimestamps`, predicate literals and query arguments over every type
was byte-identical before and after, except the two refusal sentences above. `WireColumn.fst`,
`ColumnRefinement.fst` and their differentials hold unchanged. A differential holds `readCell` and
`writeCell` to the one-row document through `decodeJson` and `encodeJson` at every type, and a query test
round-trips a literal of each of the ten types with its bytes.

**Rejected.**
- Rows that also carry `Compare` and `Token`. Nothing reads them yet, and `Cell.compare` / `token` cannot
  read a row compiled after them. The adopter that needs them adds them with its first read.
- An element loop in the row, a scan or a fill per type. It would restore the seven loops the table
  exists to remove, and it is the polymorphic shape D145.5 measured.

## 2026-10-19 — D175: the collecting decoders read every nested position through one record of overridable decoders, passed to itself; `decode*All` is its no-override case and `decode*AllWith` takes a host's

**Status:** Live

Phase 541, from the refuted premise of fuaran#2255. Since Phase 377 (`0.35.2`) and Phase 460 (`0.38.1`)
the generator's collecting decoders were public at their ROOTS only: `decode<Tag>SpecAll` and
`decodeNodeJsonAll` took the JSON value and read every nested node, union and record through the
module's private `col*` decoders. A host that delegated one family's structure therefore decoded the
whole subtree beneath it with none of its own policy; on the UI corpus that is where 24 of the 100
divergences between fuaran-dotnet's hand decoder and the generated one sit (fuaran#2255's probe over the
498 node-decoder fixtures). The TypeScript host had already solved the shape by hand with a per-member
override table (fuaran#2073).

**D175.1 — the seam is a record of decoders, open-recursive, not a functor.** Under
`Gen.Derivation.SpecDecoders` the module now emits `type CollectingDecoders`, one field per type the
vocabulary reaches through a nested position — `Node`, every non-generic union, every record, every
kind spec that is not a host projection — each typed `CollectingDecoders -> JVal -> Result<'T,
DecodeError list>`. Every collecting decoder takes the record as its first argument and reads each
nested position through it (`__ov.<Type> __ov`). `collectingDecoders` is the record of the generated
decoders. A host overrides a type by copying it — `{ collectingDecoders with Node = fun self j ->
collectingDecoders.Node self j |> policy }` — and the decoder it wrote is then the one applied at that
type at every depth, because the generated structure beneath it is handed `self`. The record takes
itself as an argument rather than closing over itself, so no recursive value is needed, nothing is
reflected over, and the emission is Fable-clean (a record of curried functions).
The alternative the shard named, a functor-style module, has no F# form: F# has no ML functors, so it
would be a class whose constructor takes the overrides and whose members re-emit the whole collecting
group, which is the same threading at a second copy of the group, and a host would override by
inheritance rather than by record copy. It was not built.

**D175.2 — measured.** Over the derivations vocabulary (`DeriveIdl`), the emitted module grows from 959
to 1,006 lines: the record type (one line per slot), the generated record (one line per slot) and one
`…With` entry per non-projected kind and per node entry; no existing declaration is duplicated. The
no-override path pays one record-field read per nested position. Timed over a 2.3 MB tree (27,306 nodes,
`decodeNodeJsonAll`, median of nine runs of twenty, with the short-circuiting `decodeNodeJson` in the
same process as the control) on a machine running other gates, the quietest runs read 15.8 to 17.8 ms
before and 17.4 to 18.6 ms after, while the untouched control read 14.7 to 16.1 ms in both: a cost of at
most about a tenth on the no-override path, inside the run-to-run spread, and none on any other path.
The falsifier is the depth tests of `IdlDeriveTests` (Phase 541): with the nested positions routed back to the private decoders,
the union and node overrides are not applied beneath the root and those two tests go red (run once in
that state).

**D175.3 — what the record does not hold.** A GENERIC union (one declaring type parameters) has no
monomorphic field: its decoder is called directly, with the record threaded through it, so every node,
union and record beneath an instantiation is still read through the record; overriding the generic
union's own structure is not offered. A projected kind's decoder is the host projection's, a leaf with no
position beneath it, so it has no field and no `…With` entry. A declared case REFINE no longer re-reads
its case with the short-circuiting decoder once every member collected: its members are collected
through the record and the refine is applied to them (`cRefine`), with `dRefine`'s refusal, code and
position unchanged, so a refined case is built from the overridable decoders' values as every other
case is.

**D175.4 — additive.** `decode<Tag>SpecAll`, `decodeNodeJsonAll` and `decodeNodeAll` keep their
signatures and answers (they read through `collectingDecoders`, and a test holds both routes equal on
clean and defective input); `decode<Tag>SpecAllWith`, `decodeNodeJsonAllWith` and `decodeNodeAllWith`
are new beside them. No `Gen.*` signature moves and no wire byte moves. A regenerated module gains the
record, so a consumer's own type named `CollectingDecoders` in the same module would collide, as a
consumer type named `NodeWitness` already does. It rides the `0.39.0` draft.

## 2026-10-19 — D176: the F* model is printed from `Decl`'s wire reach, models a hosted slot at its declared wire, and admits a default only through `Decl.literal`

**Status:** Live

**Recorded by Phase 525.** Phase 525 (the redesign pass's B §8 S9, defects D4 and D5; carries Phase 511's task 2). Before it, the F* target resolved a vocabulary by its own slot walk (`resolve`, `walk`, `Closure`, `members`, and a fresh walk per kind in `partition`). That walk modelled every hosted slot as a verbatim `jval` and decided default admissibility for itself. So the round trip was proved over a decoder looser than the hosts' in two places: a declared hosted wire form, which the F# and TypeScript decoders check (Phase 252), and an enum default spelled by its host case name, which the F# backend has refused since Phase 292.

**D176.1 — the reach is `Decl`'s, as a WIRE reach in first-reach order.** `Decl` gains `Wire: WireReach`: the closed (monomorphised) types a model of the wire declares, in first-reach order from the node envelope and then the selected kinds. Records and union instances are placed when first met and lists and maps after their element; enums are kept in first-reach order. Host-only fields reach nothing, and a hosted slot reaches its declared wire form. It is a second walk inside `Decl`, beside the host reach, because it answers a different question: the host reach is the set of declarations the host SOURCE must state, including those named only by a signature or a host-only field, in declaration order; the wire reach is what crosses the wire, monomorphised, in an order the model prints. The F* target keeps only a projection. It translates each reached declaration in reach order, and a kind is refused with the first refusal met in that order. The order is the one the old walk produced (D174.2), so every model of a vocabulary without the two defects is byte-identical. `partition` is the model of each kind alone, one resolution per selection, and no longer a walk of its own.

**D176.2 — a hosted slot is modelled as every host decodes it.**
- A declared wire form is modelled AT that form.
- A form no host can read is refused with the hosts' own refusal (`hostedWireRefusal`).
- A declared string format is refused by name (`UnmodellableInFStar`): the model's string carries no format predicate, and a model that ignored the format would accept what every host refuses. Modelling the predicate is open; lifting the refusal is a later measured decision.
- A slot with no declared wire form stays a verbatim `jval` (the known disagreement D109.5 names).

**D176.3 — one default admissibility, `Decl.literal`, read by the F# and F* backends.** It returns a typed internal `Literal` (string, int, float, bool, enum host case, empty list, record, union case), or the `UnsupportedDefault` refusal every backend gives. `FSharpDefaults.fsDefaultLit` and the F* `defaultLit` only print what it admits. The F* target refuses an admitted number as its own boundary (opaque `num` / `flt`), never as an admissibility question. The F* target used to admit four defaults the F# backend refused, and now refuses them: an enum host-case name, an empty map, a closure or opaque value, and a transparent case. A record or union literal's fields stay as authored; the presence rules that read them (host-only, absent-required) are the printers', and remain Phase 524's.

**Rejected:**
- Moving the model to declaration order. It would move every committed model and the UI tier's, and re-prove them, for no change in meaning.
- Promoting `FStarTarget.Slot` into `Decl`. `Slot` is public, so promoting it renames it in `api/`, and lifting the public types is Phase 524's breaking cut.
- Modelling a format predicate in F* now.

## 2026-10-19 — D177: what a skeleton op finds in a tree is located once, in an internal per-op view every reader reads; the script loops are one runner; the view stays internal until a reader outside `Fuaran.Core.Ops` needs it

**Status:** Amended-by D181

**Recorded by Phase 512.** `src/Fuaran.Core.Ops/Ops.fs` (`OpScope`, `OpView`, `ScriptRun`, `Ops.view`, `check`, `edit`, `applyView`, `run` / `batch` / `script` / `dryRun`, `invert`, `footprintIn`'s resolution, `createdPairs`), `WriteGate.fs` (`targetsOf`, `decide` over one walk), `Footprint.fs` (the builders are the pure clauses); rides the `0.39.0` draft (docs/releases/0.39.0.md, Internal).

**Context.** What a skeleton op does to a tree was located by every reader for itself: the engine's validators (a move ran the keyed-position search twice, once in its own check and once in the inner remove's, and the remove arm searched for the source parent its check had just walked past), the base-aware footprint (D166) through its own `tryFind` / `parentOf`, the write gate's destroyed subtree through a third, the grammar clause through `tryFind` on the trees before and after, and `invert` through five `Option.get` after a `canApply`. The gate also located each op apart from the reducer it stepped. Ten loops spelled "thread a tree through ops, stop at the first refusal".

**Decision.** (1) One internal record, `OpView`, holds what a non-batch op finds in one tree — the node it addresses, a move's destination, a remove's or move's structural source parent, and the keyed position (holder and index) holding a target that has no structural parent — located by ONE function, `Ops.view`, over an internal `OpScope` (edit witness, locate witness, keyed positions, id witness: the quadruple the validators threaded). The engine checks from it and edits through it; `footprintIn` reads its resolution from it and threads the very view it read through the engine (the keyed form locates structurally for the resolution, exactly as D166 shipped, and steps the keyed engine); `WriteGate` decides on it and steps the reducer through the same view; the grammar reads the pairs a step creates from it on the tree BEFORE the step; `invert` reads its pre-state nodes from the view `check` accepted, with total refusals where the `Option.get` were. (2) What an op NAMES, tree-blind, stays the pure footprint, pinned by the `ops/` vectors and `TreeOps.fst`'s `op_fp`; the public builders `Footprint.removeNode` / `moveTo` now ARE its remove and move clauses rather than mirrors held to it by the suite. (3) One runner, `run`, threads a step through a script and stops at the first refusal; `batch` (all-or-nothing) and `script` (first refusal wins, prefix kept, `ScriptRejection`) are its two readings, and every sequence form is one of them — `Batch`, `applyAllWith`, the dry runs, `invert`'s batch and `invertAll`, the checked engine's batch and script, the gate's `targetsOf` and `decide`. `applyChecked` / `applyAllChecked` stay as private forwarders until the policy slice removes them. (4) All three types are INTERNAL, as D171's writer and D174's `Decl` are: no reader outside `Fuaran.Core.Ops` exists yet, and the redesign's public `Scope` / `Policy` (the next slice) is where a public shape is decided. (5) `Index.afterOp` reads only the view's tree-blind part (the graft): its cost contract is "never a walk of the tree", and a located view is one, so its index-level `Track` and its rebuild fallback (which keeps the law true for an index the caller got wrong) stay.

**Consequences.** No verdict, refusal, footprint or public member moves; the `ops/` vectors and `TreeOps.fst` are byte-identical. The gate's targets are, by construction and now by test, `footprintIn`'s writes less a source parent the op does not itself name (D138), so arbitration's independence check and the gate's lock read one location of each op. Phase 492's keyed-position refusal can name the position the view located; Phase 517's `check` can ask `CanHold` of every parent the view names; Phase 518's keyed `Diff` emits ops this engine checks through the same view. The keyed-lock limit (a lock on a holder does not reach its keyed subtree) is unchanged: the gate locates through the plain scope, and a keyed gate needs the domain's keyed witness at the gate's entry, which is Phase 517's.

## 2026-10-19 — D174: the IDL emitters print from one internal resolution, `Decl`; reached declarations print in declaration order; a layout is decided once and printed per backend

**Status:** Amended-by D176

Phase 511 (the redesign pass's B §8 S2, S4 and S12). Before it, the declaration graph was computed by
each emitter that needed it: the reach walk (`Reach.referenced`, run once by the F# module, twice by
the TypeScript module, once by the declaration file and once by the derived members), the
message-carrying fixpoint, the wire-equality fixpoint, the node-holder fixpoint, the generic-union
instantiation worklist and the hosted-slot sweeps, each in its own file, and an `IdlIndex` nothing called.

**D174.1 — one resolution, internal.** `Decl.resolve idl projections kindTags` builds the `Decl` record
once per emission and every module emitter takes it (`Decl.declared` for the whole-vocabulary targets,
the JSON schema and `fsharpTypes`, which state every declaration). It is `internal`: nothing outside
this repository needs it, and Phases 524 and 525 build on it here; publishing it ahead of an outside
adopter would freeze an unused contract (D51; D171 is the precedent). The `Gen.*` signatures do not move.
The suite reaches it through the package's friend grant to `Fuaran.Core.Tests`, to state its laws.

**D174.2 — the orders are the ones the emitters always printed.** Reached enums, unions and records are
in DECLARATION order (the reach is a set, filtered over the declarations) and the selected kinds in the
caller's order. The redesign pass described the F# order as first-reach; measured, the F# module has
always printed the declaration-filtered order, and only the F* target walks in first-reach order, by its
own slot walk. A change to either order moves every committed generated artefact.

**D174.3 — the F* target's slot walk stays its own until Phase 525.** The F* model resolves IDL types to
monomorphised slots with its own presence encoding and refusals; replacing that walk with `Decl` changes
what it reads (`h.Wire`, the default literal's admissibility) and so the proof models, which is Phase
525's slice with its proof-leg re-run. `Decl` already carries the instantiation rule the two will share
(`Decl.instantiations`, named by `Decl.instName`).

**D174.4 — TypeScript derivation admission (D6 of the pass).** The TypeScript backend's admission is
`FSharpCodec.admitDerivations` over its own resolution, which declares no host projections because a
projection is F# source and the TypeScript host has none. That is what it computed before; the defect
was the documentation's claim that it admits "exactly when the F# path admits it", which held only for
a vocabulary without projections. Passing the F# projections to the TypeScript entry points would need a
new `Gen` parameter and would make the TypeScript backend refuse a derivation over a record it never
emits.

**D174.5 — presence and layout.** Each backend's encoder has one presence rule for a field's piece
(`FSharpCodec.presencePiece`, `TypeScriptCodec.tsPresencePiece`), read with whatever expression binds the
field. A union case's layout (`CaseLayout.Tagged` or `Bare`, the refusal of a bare case without exactly
one field carried as a value) and the node envelope's (`KindPlacement.NestedUnder "kind"` or `Merged`,
with its members) are decided at resolution and read by the encoders, decoders, collecting decoders, the
declaration file and the schema's `Node`. The literal half of presence (the value a field takes in a
default record, a smart constructor, a scaffold or an F* default) is the typed `Literal` of the pass's
model; its admissibility is Phase 525's and its per-backend printing Phase 524's.

**D174.6 — what this makes of Phase 474.** Its three constructs become: (1) a flattened sub-record is a
resolution step, the sub-record's members inlined into the enclosing object layout, so no printer sees a
nested key; (2) a record-payload case is a case layout whose payload is a record, printed by each
backend's object printer at the case arm; (3) a presence-keyed union is a third case/union layout beside
`Bare`, decided once with its synthesised members and its both-present refusal, and printed where `Bare`
is printed today: the F# and TypeScript encoders, decoders and collecting decoders, the schema's union
definition, and (after 525) the F* model.

## 2026-10-19 — D173: `Function` references `Propagation`, so the pipeline's dirty set is the proved closure; the three capture-key grammars are data behind one builder; the evaluators are one body over a `Scope`; each `AiSurface` verb has one guarded form

**Status:** Amended-by D186

**Recorded by Phase 510.** `Fuaran.Core.Function` (`CapabilityPipeline.fs`, `Capability.fs`, the project file), `Fuaran.Core.Query` (`Query.fs`), `Fuaran.Core.Tree` (`Hash.fs`), `Fuaran.Core.Propagation`, `Fuaran.Core.AiSurface`; rides the `0.39.0` draft (docs/releases/0.39.0.md, Additive). The `api/` baselines of `AiSurface`, `Propagation` and `Tree` gain members and lose none; `Function`'s and `Query`'s do not move. No journalled key, refusal sentence or wire byte moves.

**D173.1 — the edge, and why it is not a D2 exception.** `Fuaran.Core.Function` gains a project (and so a package) reference to `Fuaran.Core.Propagation`. D2 decides that `OpStream` and `Wire` are standalone, so a consumer of either pays for nothing else; it never made `Function` standalone — `Function` has referenced `Tree`, `Ops`, `Wire` and `OpStream` since it was cut. `Propagation` references only `Tree` and `Ops`, both already under `Function`, is FSharp.Core-only and Fable-clean, so the edge adds one package to `Function`'s graph and nothing transitively; the packed `Fuaran.Core.Function` nuspec lists `Fuaran.Core.Propagation` at the same version. There is no cycle: `Propagation` references nothing above `Ops`. The README's dependency sentence, which the suite holds to the project files, carries the edge.

**D173.2 — `dirtySet` is the closure, not a copy of it.** `CapabilityPipeline.dirtySet` was `Propagation.dependents` and `closureOver` written again, held equal to them by nothing. It is now `Propagation.dirtyFromChangedIds` over the pipeline's dependency map (each node id to the upstream ids its `FromNode` edges name; a repeated id to the union of its nodes' edges, which is what the copy computed), so `CapabilityPipeline.evalFrom` re-invokes exactly the set `proofs/Propagation.fst` models, and the reference/incremental pair stays byte-identical under the existing `capabilityPipelineIncrementalLaws` certification.
